CASE_DESCRIPTION:
The turbine waste oil tank high level alarm initiated at approx 1500hrs. The AUO was dispatched to check the level in the tank and he confirmed that the level was high but no chance of overflowing.
Considered transferring oil over the waste oil purification tank, however this tank was already full. 
Contacted Altrad to inform and check whether they were aware that the tank was full and needed emptying. Person responsible had left site but message was left for the following morning.
The wider shift team conducted further checks of the waste oil recovery tank systems to confirm that there was nothing draining such as oil cooler / coalescers etc. Nothing concerning was found across the four units.
At approx. 1930hrs it was observed that the turbine waste oil tank was overflowing.
Immediate action was taken to contain the oil within the local area and prevent ingress into the drains.
Altrad Boiler Ops were contacted to provide support with cleaning and responded quickly with a gulper. The oil spill and spill-dri was cleared.
The source of the problem was identified as a steam / water leak on  Unit 4 spray water booster pump which was causing the turbine waste oil tank to fill with water. This was balancing into the MBFP waste oil recovery tank, which in turn was being pumped into the turbine waste oil tank.
The unit 4 turbine waste oil tank was in a barriered area (associated with the leak causing the problem) and was consequently not checked as part of the operational check associated with the high level.
The turbine waste oil tank was covered with a tarpaulin to prevent further water ingress.
The site services team were contacted to arrange further support to assist the night shift with the follow up cleaning and lowering of the waste oil tank level below the high level alarm and monitoring / gulping of the main reject tunnel station water drainage of any carry over oil which was completed.
TITLE: Main turbine hall waste oil tank

CASE_DESCRIPTION: On Friday morning, a report was received to the outage office that there was oil dripping from the Coalescer drain separator vessel.  On investigation it was found that the Coalescer vent valve had been opened slightly.  The oil issuing into the Coalscer drain had eventually overcome the drains separator, and spilled a small amount of oil onto the basement floor.  The vent was closed immediately upon discovery.  It is not known how long, when or for what reason the vent was opened, but it is presumed it had been unintentionally knocked by a person or object at some point that morning.  There was no operational reason to operate or move the valve, and no-one was in the vicinity of the Coalscer when the open vent was discovered and closed.   The jacking oil pumps, oil tank and Coalescer were all available for normal service and at NWP.

CASE_DESCRIPTION:
During the Fall Arrest inspection yesterday, Integral delivered a new harness for inspection, which failed. The Inspector noted that some of the catches were the wrong way round and while this isn’t a failing in itself it would make the harness uncomfortable to wear, as the catches would rub on the chest of anyone wearing it. 
As this was a new harness the Inspector added it to the system and then did a thorough check of all the details provided on the label. He found that the harness was manufactured in India in 2024, but only showed a CE safety marking, which is no longer valid for new items in the UK since 2023. This means that the harness is illegal as there’s no proof it has been tested to the correct UK CA standard. 
Inquires were made about where the harness was purchased from and no records have been found so far.
When I spoke to Facilities later they didn’t remember ordering a harness for Integral, and were going to investigate.
Facilities don't keep their own inspection register.
TITLE: Harness/fall arrest inspection by British Engineering Services - Harness found with the wrong safety markings

CASE_DESCRIPTION:
On the 28th February noticed puffs of black smoke being emitted from GRU 30 stack, not long after the Rich TEG feed had been introduced and on the following day the unit tripped on low reboiler pressure, again as the Rich TEG feed was being established._x000D_
_x000D_
The PI trend for the low pressure trip on the 1st March follows a very similar pattern to the trips observed in February & March 2020 and at the time wetter than normal Rich TEG was put forward as a possible explanation for a large spike in the reboiler pressure. However, the upstream GDU moisture analyser EKC10CQ001 wasn’t operating at the time which made this quite speculative._x000D_
_x000D_
One possible explanation for this could be the residual wetter than normal TEG held up in the contactors (approximately 14 m3) which would be transferred to the Rich Buffer tank in the subsequent withdrawals during which time it would be made partially drier by the incoming TEG although this would still have quite a high moisture content._x000D_
_x000D_
While the wet TEG theory remains far from conclusive it now has more credibility and GRU 30 was operated on the 2nd March with a Rich TEG feed which probably contained a more normal moisture content and no operating issues were observed.
TITLE: GRU 30 incomplete combustion event and reboiler low pressure trip

CASE_DESCRIPTION:
First Incident:  4/12/2021
CPU 1 was undergoing start up after SW 30 shutdown. Almost at the end of start-up activity the following happened:
1.	At 0110hrs received Furnace Non Urgent Alarm in DCS.
2.	On checking at furnace BMS panel by operator, found Naphtha KOD level was around 10% and continuously dropping, but instead of appearing LAL-1711 and LALL-1711, the displayed alarm was LAH-1711 and LAHH-1711.
3.	Furnace firing was stopped immediately from DCS and Field Operator (FO) was rushed to field to check for any leak.
4.	Checked physically at site and found the naphtha KOD was full.
Action Taken
1.	Vessel drained and reduced the level to reset LAH-1711 and LAHH-1711
2.	Drained LIT-1711 and LIT-1713 LP and HP impulse lines
3.	Reset the alarm in BMS panel and restarted the furnace
4.	Observed the KOD vessel level control cut-in and cut-off working well.
Second Incident: 4/12/2021
1.	At 1615 hrs Non urgent alarm appeared on SCADA.
2.	1615 hrs checked in Furnace PLC for alarm details, it was showing LAL-1711 (13 %) and continued going down trend.
3.	At that point of time Naphtha flow to furnace was 1.2 TPH and P-004 to KOD was 1.9 TPH (KOD  level control XV open and close function was ok throughout shift).
4.	KOD level continue decreasing, informed FO to increased flow to KOD to prevent furnace Naphtha pump tripping on LAL-1711. (16:19 to 16:21 hrs).
5.	At 1621 hrs LALL-1711 appear  in PLC and furnace Naphtha pump got tripped on LL but furnace not tripped and continue firing with 250Kg/hr flow rate.
6.	Furnace temperature continued to go down, so unit kept on long circulation at 1630 hrs and later kept on short circulation.
7.	Informed FO to check KOD physically, FO found KOD was over filled.
8.	Stop Naphtha feeding to KOD by closing XV-322.
9.	KOD emptied out.
Similar third and fourth incident happened on 6/12/2021 at 0145 hrs and on 14/12/2021 at 1152 hrs respectively
TITLE: Furnace Trip due to Naphtha KOD tank overfilled.

The spray from the Leak was localised to C16 / C17 burner, but the excess has tracked down the pipework and steel work to the boiler basement.

It is unclear at what time the leak developed, but was not identified by the end of Saturday Day shift when the burner front was checked at approx 15:00hrs. 
The fuel oil had ran down the lower levels of the burner front, into the snake pit and Into the boiler basement adjacent 'C' pa fan.   As soon as the leak was discovered, the drain between 'C' PA fan and the ash hopper was plugged, and dresser dry applied to the immediate area.  Dresser dry was then applied to the higher levels where ever the oil had pooled.  Air heater wash sump, ash fines pits and ash crusher pits have showed no signs of oil as of 09:30 04/12/22.
TITLE: PSNH - U1 C16 Oil Burner hose leak

CASE_DESCRIPTION:

The unit was synchronised and proceeded to load up, at approx. 440MW Hot Re-heater safety valve 166 lifted as a result of the intercept valve being tripped. Although the HP exhaust pressure was only 40 bar, indicating the safety valve had lifted “light” (there are also 4 other R/htr safety valves passing on this unit)._x000D_
The unit load was reduced to 230MW initially thus reducing R/htr pressure and enable a gag to be installed, unsuccessful the load had to be reduced further to 20MW allowing successful fitting of the gag. Unit load was then returned back to full capacity. _x000D_

When the pressure in the lines dropped the fire system was discharged in the oil storage area.  This deluge caused damage to several boxes of grease cartridges and also allowed oil drip trays to overflow.  The contents of which went down the station drains.

Oily water also proceeded to pass through to the office area and into the switchroom and down a cable tunnel.

This was not discovered properly until Tuesday 18th Feb as the Altrad oil supervisor was working in the main stores on Monday 17th Feb and didn't go in to the oil stores.  Legacy issues with the fire alarm system prevented the Operation teams from identifying where the mulsifyre system had been discharged and led them to believe there was a significant leak.

Please note this draw pit has not been deemed as a Confined space .


I contacted Trant Engineering Civils Manager and asked him to attend site immediately of which he did, discussion with myself and Civils Manager and points noted agreed as per next paragraph

Lack of barriers demarcating the work area, no safety A frame or harness in place, no second man above ground, gas monitor not being worn and 4 inches of water in the draw pit.

Trant Engineering 755-TEL-XX-XX-MS-C-0057 Rescue Plan not being adhered to.


Civils Manager instructed his employees to  replace the covers and stop work.

Please see attached photographs

IP steam system Safety Valves lifted. (ST out of service, HP bypass valve Open)._x000D_
At the DCS the IP bypass system spray water Valve recorded 90% Open but with little or no flow. _x000D_
At -3MW Generated Load a GT Trip was initiated from the Unit Desk._x000D_
The IP Safety Valves closed almost immediately._x000D_

CASE_DESCRIPTION:
Up until 2014 site had a problem in the Winter with the wellheads tripping on low temperature when the wellhead flow control valve was closed, usually when the DCS Stop or Adjustable Setpoint were reached at Pmin or Pmax. 

This trapped the gas between the wellhead and the control valve stopping the normal convection flows of warmer gas between the caverns. 

If the ambient temperature was below zero this static gas would cool to 0 degrees and activate the low temperature wellhead trip which is only intended to prevent low gas temperatures in the cavern and production tubing caused by a large, prolonged withdrawal.

To remedy this problem the trip was made ‘smart’ and was only activated if the flow control valve was open and it was deactivated when the valve was closed and no withdrawal could be occurring but this required a closed limit indication adding to the actuators. (see attached)

Since then 8 replacement actuator controllers were ordered that don’t come with the limits as standard and they have been in the stores for some time until one was fitted on H403 and were identified that the limits (there may have been an open limit fitted too) were missing.

The absence of the closed limit switch would not create a hazard and it would just generate the potential for an unnecessary trip.

This has been recorded as it is a case of a like for like replacement that isn’t.
TITLE: Like for like actuator issue

CASE_DESCRIPTION:
An initial problem was detected with the GRUs where they were quickly dumping >6m3 hour of cold teg into the regen units on start up, which if wet could lead to a pressure trip. A modification was prepared for tuning out some poor control on the flow limiter on the stripping column.  However, it was not implemented because on closer inspection, the Rich TEG buffer vessel level Operator-adjustable set point was sitting at a low level.  Increasing the set point from 380 mm to 500 mm smoothed the start up process and prevented the pressure trips.

After a period of time, Operators detected that during the shut down of the GRUs, the TEG HP pumps were repeatedly turning on and off.  Investigation identified that this was because the auto-changeover setpoint of 1m3/hr was now being matched by the flow of Rich TEG from the buffer tank due to the changed setpoint (as described above).

There was no safety consequence to the pumps repeatedly changing over.  However, there was a potential plant damage risk.  Hence, this observation has been raised to determine any additional learning relating to the sites control of modification set points, including operator adjustable set points.
TITLE: Unanticipated effect from altered Operator set point

CASE_DESCRIPTION:
There have been multiple cases of low level hydrogen leaks detected on both SC10 and SC20 synchronous condensers during offline periods.

July 7th 2022

The synchronous condenser was shutdown due to the need for a Mod 2 400KV grid isolation for maintenance activities.

Whilst the SC20 Generator was at standstill a hydrogen leak alarm was received on the gas detector panel CYE01 in the Killingholme control room. Investigations at that time could not detect a genuine leak although the reading appeared to last for approximately 30 seconds and peaked at 20% LEL. This alarm was detected at both ends of the Generator on both HD005 and HD006. 

Later as the Hydrogen Purity Concentration procedure was being carried out these alarms were received again. This time a noticeable leak could be heard within the turbine hall also. These readings peaked at 40% LEL and the detection lasted for several minutes. 

To clarify the first alarm was received with the shaft at standstill and no work being carried out and the second alarm was received when the shaft was still at standstill but hydrogen filling was taking place.

A further leak alarm was detected when  SC20 was put on barring up to 200RPM using the oil system

Aug 21st 2022

Again a 400KV outage was required for maintenance activities on MOD1.

Again, Killingholme OPS took the opportunity to attempt to sweeten the generator hydrogen purity. There were similar leaks of hydrogen detected as there was on SC20 above but in slightly different.

* Whilst at standstill during the H2 sweetening process

* Whilst at standstill following completion of the sweetening process.

* Whilst on barring on the return to operation

19/12/2022

Leak alarms were once again raised when SC20 was stopped to carry out repairs on GT21 GCB.  Leaks stopped once the unit was put back on barring.
TITLE: SC10/20 Generator Hydrogen Leak alarms.

CASE_DESCRIPTION:
Recently at Ratcliffe we've taken delivery of 600 new HID access control cards.  As of last month our previously issued E.On access control cards ran out and we started issuing from the new batch.

After a few days a couple of users informed us that when setting up SecurePrint on their new cards, when scanning in on the printers instead of taking them through the registration process it logged them in as another user.

We believe that this is due to the stored numbers on the two active people's different cards being the same, and/or SecurePrint not using the site code portion of the access control cards.

This is a data protection risk as there is a chance that these users with duplicate card numbers could print sensitieve personal data off the SecurePrint queue from that account that they are incorrectly logged into.

I've attached a flow diagram to explain the problem.

Fundamentally we believe that the fragmented way that Access Control cards are issued across the company and having a company wide access control card swipe system for the printers is why the risk of duplicate numbers on Access control cards is a data protection risk.

There is also a potential that these duplicate cards could allow someone access to another site that they are not authorised, but we don't believe this risk is high as the access control systems should use the site codes as well, but this will need investigating.
TITLE: Potential for Duplicate Swipe Card Numbers to be allocated with different Access Control Cards

CASE_DESCRIPTION:
During a run up to FSNL. _x000D_
21:22 Bearing 2 vib > max 1 alarm. DCS showed 20mm/s but this is the max of its range. GE suggested the GT should have tripped automatically but it didn't. _x000D_
21:23 GT reached FSNL and vibration has dropped_x000D_
_x000D_
The reason for the GT not tripping on high vibration was investigated. The Bentley Nevada set points were checked and the trip levels are set at 14.7 when the GT trip matrix says they should be 11.8. With the 1.5x mulitplier on start up the 14.7 became 22.05 which was above the range of the instrument (20mm/s) so the GT did not trip. Once at FSNL the multipliers are not in effect so the trip limit was back to 14.7. _x000D_
_x000D_
Further investigation required.
TITLE: GT vibration trip setting

CASE_DESCRIPTION:
Unit 1 desync 2025hrs, Unit 4 sync 2207hrs, Unit 2 desync 2255hrs.
At 2254hrs Aux Boilers 210, 240 & 250 tripped due to a fleeting gas detector (Steam Generator 2 Gas Detector).
Until the Boiler system and gas slam shut valve could be reset the aux steam header was supplemented from Units 1 & 2, manually,  via SVAPCV019. This initially resulted in an momentary over pressurisation of the Auxiliary Steam Headers up to18Bar, (0*-SVA-025-PT).  Unit 3 Auxiliary Steam Header was isolated and depressurised for outage and so unaffected.
The Aux Steam header then dropped to 2 Bar before Aux Boilers 220 and 230 began loading enough to raise the pressure.
This resulted in the condenser pressures of Unit 1 reaching 165mBar and Unit 2 301mBar due to low gland steam pressures. Unit 4 vacuum was unaffected.
The Gas Treatment Plant was being started at the time of the trip, which required some venting of the compressor HP suction drum V403, and the wind was from the west (this may or may not relate to the gas detector trip).

The Unit Auxiliary Steam Header Safety Valves PSV003 are rated to lift at 18Bar according to the P&ID.
TITLE: Station and Unit Auxiliary steam header over pressurisation.

CASE_DESCRIPTION: I was looking to assess a Maintenance Order for set up actuator unit 4 FSR-UV -051. The operational line is for setting up the actuator and the long text stated set up actuator and adjust limits and torque settings. There is no safe system of work in the long text so i had a look at the PRT which is for generic Kaefer actuator stroke check fault find which allows them to carry out a full range of jobs including IR and balance checks,replacement of components and boards etc. If I had assessed this job on the long text the competent person would have had a Safety Document that i thought was for stroke checking the actuator but the method of work allows them to possibly do much more work. In my opinion there should be something written in to GMI SHE 003 which makes it clear that the work scope and method of work that an SAP assesses for the job from the long text needs to match any PRT.
TITLE: Maintenance Order discrepancy between operational line description and PRT.

CASE_DESCRIPTION:
The safety isolation key for the Upsurge Control Valve No.515 Control Air valve was released from the T3B cascade key safe following the return of the T3B PFW.  The release of this key (safety key No 9727) allowed us to prepare for the PFW ROMP (Permit For Work with Restoration Of Motive Power), for the re-connection of the valve 515 and setting of the valve limits.   Following release of the key on the morning of the 13/07, the Outage Commissioning operative was asked to attach a ROMP notice to the valve in preparation for the issue of the safety document.  On getting to the valve location it was noted that there was no isolation lock on the valve as expected.  The chain that was used to isolate the valve was still attached to the valve body / pipework but there was no sign of the isolation lock.
The control valve and actuator had both been removed & replaced during the Outage period.  The air pipework and the valve spindle had both been disconnected to allow the removal / replacement of the valve / actuator.  The air isolation valve was not directly local to the valve, it was the master isolator approx 6ft away on the adjacent wall.
The Authorised Persons Isolation sheet was checked, and the isolation point had been double checked and double signed for at the start of the Outage period when the T3B cascade box was established; on release of the safety key from the key safe the signatures were crossed off of the AP sheet.  The immediate area was searched for any sign of a broken / damaged lock, but nothing could be found.
TITLE: U4 Upsurge Control Valve No515 Control Air Valve missing isolation lock

CASE_DESCRIPTION:
A PFW safety document for U4 ‘Y’ 3.3KV SW/BRD maintenance was issued on Monday 16th May (AM) to one of the electrical CP’s.

The CP (Competent Person) proceeded to work on the 3.3KV ‘Y’ board during the coarse of the day, carrying out VCB maintenance, CCT spout maintenance and function checks as per his maintenance orders and maintenance procedures and PFW.  At the end of the working day the CP surrendered the PFW and explained to the duty SAP (Senior Authorised Person) the state of the works and progress made.  During the discussion the CP stated that the VCB’s had been returned to the Earth position.  
To allow the VCB’s to return to the CCT earth position, requires the 110v solenoid fuses to be available; but the duty SAP noted the fuses were quoted as a POI on the safety document.

In discussion with the SAP who prepared the safety document - During the preparation stage, he had read & understood that the electrical method, stated 110v supplies were needed to function check the VCB closing springs, & that the VCB’s should be returned to the as found position following cct spout maintenance.  

Because of this, the preparing SAP had made supplies available to the 110V solenoids for function checking, and to allow the VCB’s to be put back to the CCT earth position.  The Safety document was already pre-prepared on Nisoft quoting the Solenoid fuses as POI’s, and the Preparing SAP omitted to remove the isolation point from the POI’s list in Nisoft prior to printing.  

The safety document was cancelled and the POI on Nisoft quoting the Solenoid 110v fuses was removed.   The new Safety document was re-issued on the 17th May to continue the work.

The isolation point originally quoted – 
•	‘Y’ Unit SW/BRD 110v CONTROL FUSES & SOLENOID FUSES             WITHDRAWN & CAUTIONED

The isolation point was changed to  
•	‘Y’ Unit SW/BRD 110v CONTROL FUSES                                              
WITHDRAWN & CAUTIONED

The safety document had been pre-prepared so that an isolation list could be produced for the isolating AP.  This was a couple of weeks prior to the document being printed as the contractors were delayed in attending site.

The Solenoid isolation had been removed from the key safe, made available & crossed off of the AP sheet by the preparing SAP, but not removed from the PFW.

Please note that this Observation Synergy is being raised as a prompt to have a discussion regarding the importance of SAP's to ensure the  administrative preparation of the safety documents is given the SAP's full attention, and is prioritised, to ensure the SAP isn't distracted by non SFS procedures.
TITLE: U4 'Y' 3.3KV Switchboard

QEB10AA153 Short Description: U4 A AFCU STRM 2 SHUTOFF ISOL VLV
QEB10AA153 Long Description: U4 A SIDE SCR AMMONIA FLOW CONTROL UNIT STREAM 2 SHUTOFF VALVE INSTRUMENT AIR SUPPLY ISOLATION VALVE

HSJ10AA010 Short Description: U4 A AFCU STRM 2 PNEU SOV 
HSJ10AA010 Long Description: A SIDE SCR AMMONIA FLOW CONTROL UNIT STREAM 2 PNEUMATIC SHUTOFF VALVE

The associated permit (already cancelled) 2022/2309/SP used a correct functional location description for the work intended although did not reference KKS HSJ10AA010 :

TITLE: SSOW - U4 AFCU Steam 2 Shut Off Valve - Notification & WOC with incorrect SAP FL

CASE_DESCRIPTION:
11 Oct 2022 Morning time : Enfield CCGT unit was on base load at appx. 390 MW

11;20 Duty shift operation technician during his second plant checks, noticed oil puddle in steam turbine basement ; On closer inspection also found oil spraying from Steam Turbine IP valve at North Side. 

Followed the leak to Turbine floor: Oil was found to be spraying from test pressure gauge on ST IP Stop Valve North Side.
 
Oil leak was immediately contained, REMIT declared & informed traders, Steam turbine controlled shutdown carried out, informed engineering and security gatehouse to prepare for evacuation & rollcall if required

Oil leak stopped once the steam turbine IP Stop Valve shut, Engineering team investigated, found test pressure gauge bourdon tube ruptured and oil leaking out from the damaged bourdon tube. Removed the pressure gauge, rectified oil leak 

Leak from hot surfaces and surrounding areas then cleaned, pipes lagging inspected and claddings cleaned from leaked & accumulated oil in lagging insulation,  

Gas turbine was kept ON during this time on bypass mode. Once the oil leak was rectified, REMIT declared and unit was brought back to base load.
TITLE: Steam Turbine IP Stop Valve  (North) Power oil leak

Valve locations identified on plant and valves with these labels were closed. on closing 01FSRHV927 it was observed that 'A' transmitter was lost on DCS and leak did not stop. CASE_DESCRIPTION:
On Monday 27th September at approx 0830, a Permit For Work ROMP ( Restoration of Motive Power) was issued from the Outage permit for work office to allow the set-up of limits and stroking of pneumatic valve 255 following outage works.  At the time of issue the boiler was being set up for a Hydraulic test.  As per normal procedure and prior to the hydraulic, all issued docs were checked and any relevant safety documents that could affect the hydraulic were suspended.  Between the times of the check of the issued documents and start of the boiler hydraulic, the ROMP for valve 255 was issued without the issuing SAP making the connection to it being affected by the boiler hydraulic.  The CP who collected the Romp proceeded to his point of work, made the air supply available and started to stroke the valve from the local junction box.  As the valve opened there was a release of pressure within the process pipework, which was 'quite loud' and caused vibration within the pipework.  This startled the CP and he proceeded to shut the control air valve immediately.   The CP reported straight to the Outage duty SAP who attended the point of work and realised the ROMP should not have been in force during the boiler hydraulic test.  The ROMP was suspended and working party withdrawn.   

The PFW ROMP specifically stated no access to the process side of the control valve / system, so the CP and working party were not at risk from the process medium.
TITLE: U1 Boiler HP Sootblower Control Valve 255.

CASE_DESCRIPTION:
ST Clutch Lube Oil supply pipe weld was commenced on Sunday morning 30th august 2020. _x000D_
On cutting the existing pipe the Doosan Tech saw more oil than he was expecting draining under head from the stub pipe he had cut, not under pressure just weiring over. _x000D_
He stopped work ,informed us and we went to investigate. _x000D_
There was quite a bit of oil in the gallery under the grating. We applied a spill kit and requested Wayne Chandler to assist cleaning it up with spill pads. _x000D_
There was about 10 litres of oil possibly that we mopped up and it stopped flowing from the stub._x000D_
We conducted a job stop and meeting with GE supervisor. jacking oil work was suspended while we established a cause._x000D_
_x000D_
 The reason for the oil draining from the pipework was the fact that the bearing pedestals had filled with oil because of the jacking oil being put into service constantly. The level would reach the supply pipework internally to the pedestal._x000D_
This then ran down the SUPPLY pipework, filling the blanked and previously drained line back to the tank.. _x000D_
It was drain under head only and a gentle weiring from the stub. It would drain and stop . when jacking oil back in service a little bit more would drain._x000D_
_x000D_
We fitted a drain hose to the cut stub pipe and this was placed into an IBC to collect any oil. Permit for Clutch supply pipe weld cancelled._x000D_
 Monday 31st August the line was drained at the supply blank and the blank removed . Lube oil pumps isolated and PFW issued to weld flange onto stub after line proved drained again.._x000D_
 _x000D_
 History;_x000D_
Supply pipework drained and Lube oil blank fitted under PFW 2020/00819 on 01/08/2020 and entered into blanks register._x000D_
Drain /return lines back to tank remained available throughout._x000D_
This was the basis for our Clutch weld job._x000D_

CASE_DESCRIPTION: During the morning commute to work I observed a Grey Audi A3, registration YM19 WNU driving very dangerously. Whilst exiting the M1 northbound at junction 24 the Audi driver decided not to join the slip road in advance and instead continued travelling in the bottom lane of the M1 making no indication that he would be exiting at the junction. He then decided that he needed to leave the M1 at J24 and dangerously came to a stop in the bottom lane of the M1 which made other drivers travelling at speed of up to 70mph take evasive action to avoid a serious collision. The driver then proceeded to make his way around the J24 roundabout towards the A453. At the traffic lights leading to the A453 (remembrance way) the driver decided to cut in front of me where there was clearly insufficient space causing me to take emergency action. The driver clearly believed that his actions were justified as when I sounded my horn he replied with a 'gesture'. I overtook the driver on the A453 and continued into the UTG carpark. I realised that the Audi driver was also travelling to site and as I parked up I saw him drive at excessive speeds between the gatehouse and the Engineering Academy which was his end destination. Within 5 minutes this driver caused 3 separate incidents on the road, all of which had the potential to be fatal.
TITLE: Dangerous Driving

CASE_DESCRIPTION: A Trainer was attending a customer site to complete apprentice observations. He arrived at site on 22nd September and completed a successful transfer to and from the wind turbine. Later in the day the team at RWE were told they had to leave the turbine within an hour and a half because the waves were getting high. The team transferred and all made it back to site safely however, Jonathan has described it as a frightening experience. RWE state safe wave height should be 2.8m but the waves on this day were over 3m. When they returned to site all RWE staff were asked to complete near hits so that they could investigate the reasons someone had authorised transfer to the wind turbine that day. As the Trainer was part of the group on site and for his own safety we wanted to raise this as a near hit within Uniper too.

CASE_DESCRIPTION:
A HGSL Operator is developing a simulator of the control system.  This work requires systematic review of the alarm arrangements across the installation.  When reviewing smoke and gas detection within the compressor enclosures, the Operator noticed that the code for the compressor to "fail safe" in the event of detector power-loss did not reflect the arrangement elsewhere on the site.  Hence, based on the operators concern that the detectors were not "fail safe", testing was undertaken on the same day to isolate the power and review the function of the code.  The test identified that the detectors were fail safe, but used a slightly different code - most likely due to the automatic EDP function found on the compressors but not elsewhere on the plant._x000D_
_x000D_

CASE_DESCRIPTION:
NDT/Radiography has been completed on a number of shifts – the process involves completing the Appendix A documentation which details important information – one being the source type and size – the source decay certificate also states type and current size – the Appendix A is prepared by the FieldCore Mechanical contractor along with the decay certificate – this is checked/signed by the Uniper Engineer and distributed to relevant parties nominated on the Appendix A – the source nominated was Iridium - Ir192 23.7._x000D_
Iris the NDT company arrived at Enfield Power station at approx. 02:00 – after a review the Shift team leader found the source was a Selenium 75 Source with a strength of 32.8 Curies. (>20Curies) – The shift team leader has been on Nights since Wednesday, I was confident in the competence of the IRIS Engineers and decided this was admin error and not that IRIS had bought the wrong Source._x000D_
Once IRIS showed the shift team leader all the necessary paperwork for the Source, he allowed the Radiography to continue._x000D_
The fact that IRIS told him during the Saturday morning testing, that they were bringing a stronger Selenium Source for Sunday’s testing, was also taken in to account.
TITLE: Incorrect paper work detailing type of radioactive NDT source planned to be used on weld testing

CASE_DESCRIPTION:
I went to Ratcliffe Power Station to carry out internal visual inspection of the U3 main steam drum (part of the 2020 Statutory outage works).  This pressure vessel is classed as a “confined space”._x000D_

Prior to entry, we were informed by staff from the mechanical contractor that there was no requirement to wear any gas monitoring / detection equipment.  The mechanical contracting staff were working in the vessel when we arrived, however they exited the vessel to enable us to carry out our inspection work._x000D_
_x000D_
Before commencing work, we confirmed the lack of gas monitor requirement with a visit to the permit office / control room._x000D_

However, because a gas monitor is specified in our RAMS, we sourced a gas monitor from the Station Chemist and conducted our work as usual with a gas monitor attached._x000D_

This appeared to be an apparent change to the sites procedures.  Personal gas monitoring / detection equipment has been considered mandatory in confined spaces of this nature in previous years and at every other site UTG work on.   _x000D_

We believe the Station has conducted a full investigation, therefore this is more for UTG learning.
TITLE: Ratcliffe Confined Space Procedures

CASE_DESCRIPTION:
On Friday 17th September it was reported that a GE/Fieldcore operative could not smell the wd40 he was using, as a precaution he took a LFT which proved positive, he left site in a controlled manner and the area sanitised, a close contact assessment completed. (He was a few days later confirmed positive by the official PCR).
3 operatives where identified and each had a LFT which all proved negative, they all had been double jabbed and were assessed able to carry on working as per Government advice.
However this against EGTL site procedure and against the instruction of the Grain Safety Team Leader who was contacted on A/L. The EGTL procedure insists that all Close Contacts should have been isolated until such time that the EGTL Appendix 9 RTW for Close Contacts had been completed. 
The Safety Team Leader did not find out until Tuesday 21st that the Close Contacts had been allowed to stay at work.
LFT have been conducted daily on the Close Contacts and surveillance and controls in place and negative results recorded.
TITLE: Coronavirus Close Contact Assessment breach of EGTL COVID-19 Procedure.

CASE_DESCRIPTION:
U7 Steam Turbine was tripped using the CCR Emergency Stop Button as per the recommissioning programme for the HP bypass works._x000D_
The HP bypass opened satisfactorily but the IP bypass tripped almost immediately after opening, it tripped on Condenser Inlet temperature >Max 2; the spraywater valve for the IP bypass failed to quench the steam temperature in sufficient time. The Operator was unable to reset the temperature trip and therefore was unable to reinstate the IP bypass valve._x000D_
Subsequently, the CRH / IP systems pressurised causing the safety valves to lift._x000D_
Owing to the IP bypass trip, the GT PLS(T), leading to desynch at 03:04hrs. The HP header pressure increased due to the GT EV burners remaining in service for cooldown. Turning Gear was selected but the fires remained in service. The HP system safety valves lifted @155barg, the GT ESB was pressed at the CCR to extinguish the burners and reduce the HP pressure._x000D_
_x000D_
The IP bypass spray valve was later investigated by the maintenance team, I'm not sure what was found and if any changes to the control system were made.
TITLE: Unit 7 Safety Valve Lifting unintentionally

CASE_DESCRIPTION:
A crane lift, of  sheeting panels onto U42 were witnessed without a tag line fitted. This caused the panels on both occasions to spin and bump into the side of the access platform and structure. No injury or damaged sustained.

CASE_DESCRIPTION:
On Sunday 23rd May 2021, a Competent person (CP) collected a safety document PFW ROMP (Restoration Of Motive Power) to work on bled steam to de-aerator valve 4002.   Following collection of the safety document, the CP proceeded to the point of work he knew as 4002 valve, but found that the safety key issued with the PFW ROMP did not match the isolation lock on the valve, and there wasn't a ROMP notice present.  
The CP contacted the duty Senior Authorised Person (SAP) immediately to report his findings.  The SAP attended the point of work and found the CP on what he believed to be the wrong valve.  The CP confirmed through his experience and knowledge that he believed he was on 4002 valve, and showed the SAP a handwritten sign on the pneumatic valve control box (approximately 12ft away from the valve it's self) stating it was valve 4002.  The duty SAP took the CP to the valve that was isolated for the ROMP, and showed him the local permanent plant ID label attached to the valve stating valve 4002.  After some discussion and consulting drawings, it was still not 100% clear which valve was 4002.  The Duty SAP cancelled the PFW ROMP and de-isolated both 4001 & 4002 valves, and asked a Unit Operator to operate the valves remotely from the ovation soft desk in the main control room.  On operation of the valves it was confirmed that the permanent plant ID label attached to U4 4002 valve was incorrect, and that the valve was actually 4001.  

After confirming that the identification on valve 4001 (stating 4002) was wrong, 4002 valve was inspected and there was no plant label attached to 4002 valve, apart from the hand written sign on the pneumatic control box which is not local to the valve. 

U4 is currently on an Interim outage, and the air supply valves for both 4001 and 4002 were isolated at the start of the outage period (approx. 2 weeks earlier).  Both valves have been worked on through the outage with 4002 requiring setting up under a PFW ROMP before being returned to service.

Information

Both 4001 and 4002 pneumatic bled steam valves are located on U4 De-aerator.  On Unit 4, 4001 valve is located on the 'B' side of the De-aerator, 4002 is located on the 'A' side.  The valves are approximately 10 meters apart, each on it's own platform.  The valves are the opposite way round on U1 & U2 compared to U3 & U4.
TITLE: SSoW - U4 pneumatic bled steam to DA valve 4002 permit for work ROMP

CASE_DESCRIPTION:
Whilst withdrawing gas from the caverns and changing load from 700,000Sm3/hr to 900,000Sm3/hr by the pressure reduction valves (PRV’s) the plant suffered an unexpected Safety Instrumented System (SIS) trip on rate of change (falling <1bar/min) on the pipeline to the National transmission system (NTS)._x000D_
_x000D_
In 2011 similar issues were experienced when certain plant conditions were met (approx. 8 bar dp between caverns and the National Transmission System [NTS] system). To prevent this from occurring a Management of Change (MoC) was implemented that allowed the shift operator control of the plant 'global gain'. This global gain effectively slows the plant control system down to prevent these large flow variances happening quickly and thus preventing demands on the SIS system. There is a standing operational instruction for the shift operator to manually change the global gain from 1 to 0.7 when in these pressure ranges._x000D_
_x000D_
On this occasion the operator had not reduced the global gain as when the withdrawal nomination commenced the conditions for the global gain to be reduced were not met, however, as these conditions are dynamic as the withdrawal nomination continued the conditions were met but the global gain was not adjusted._x000D_
_x000D_
Upon investigation of the DCS trend it appears this has been happening (to a lesser extent) for the past 16 months. This ties in with a rolling programme of overhauling each PRV, of which we have 3 off. It is thought that splitting the flow across two valves instead of three may have contributed to the issues described.
TITLE: Loss of process control resulting in plant trip

CASE_DESCRIPTION:
It appears that U6 Sequencers (HRSG/WSC and ST) stopped running(Disabled themselves) when restarting the unit from an SSD trip during unit start-up. _x000D_
It was not noticed that the sequencers were not running initially (no alarms) until the operator realised that the HP bypass had failed to open. Immediately the HP by-pass was manually switched on which resulted in the HP-pass opening to pressurise the cold re-heat line as designed. This had the result of pressurising the CRH line due to high pressure already in the HP steam line. this consequently led to the CRH safety valves lifting at their designed lift pressures. _x000D_
Just after the HP-bypass had been switched on it was then noticed that the HRSG/WSC and ST sequencers were not running, these were immediately re-started. Once the condenser vacuum had reached 300mbar, the CRH pressure was able to relieve to the condenser via the IP by-pass valve. The unit the ran up as designed.
TITLE: Uncontrolled Release of steam via safety valve.

CASE_DESCRIPTION: On Friday 14-Aug, U3 outage permit (G24 WAL) was returned in preparation for commissioning activities. On Saturday morning 15-Aug electrical commissioning of all boiler stop & bypass valves was undertook (ref. LWC 0249/SL BACTWAL) with B2 bypass vlv 114 being reported as "valve stuck". Outage permit office subsequently applied an isolation (inc. lock & tags to handwheels) to all BSV & bypass valves on Saturday pm. On Monday 17-Aug the Boiler engineer was informed of B2 bypass valve being tight by electrical team and this message was passed to valve contractor site manager to undertake further, non-intrusive, investigation. It was expected that the valve would be hand operated using handwheel only. On Tuesday 18-Aug the valve contractor confirmed they had adjusted valve packing and also decoupled the valve drive spindle to manually stroke the valve. While the current state of the boiler means there was no system derived hazard at this time, as a point of isolation, these works were not permitted at this time as no active safety document was available.
TITLE:
SSoW_x000D_
Mechanical commissioning of BSV bypass valve without valid safety document

CASE_DESCRIPTION:
On Starting my journey to site, within half a mile of my journey start, a low tyre pressure warning light appeared on the dashboard display. I stopped the vehicle and checked the tyre to see if it was noticeably deflated. It was not. I reset the monitor and continued on the journey. _x000D_
I reported to Hertz at approx. 08:30, I stopped at the motorway services, checked the tyre again and contacted Hertz when their office was open that I suspected that the hire car had been supplied with a slow puncture. I also reported unrecorded rain damage to the door cards, door handles and dash boards._x000D_
I contacted the Uniper Central Support team to record this report of pre-existing damage._x000D_
When I arrived at site, I followed up the initial report with an email with photo's of the water damage._x000D_
_x000D_
Complaints were registered with Hertz _x000D_
_x000D_
On Wednesday morning, I started my journey from hotel to site and the same tyre pressure warning appeared. this time when the tyre was inspected a clear depletion of the tyre pressure was visible. _x000D_
_x000D_
This was reported to Hertz as confirmation that the vehicle had been supplied with a slow puncture with a complaint that this is the third time that I had been supplied with a hire vehicle from Hertz with a puncture. The tyre was inflated and Hertz were notified that it would be monitored overnight. if the tyre pressure had not significantly depleted, the vehicle would be taken home for collection by Herts. However if the tyre was deflated at the morning inspection, Hertz would be instructed to change the defective vehicle with immediate effect._x000D_
_x000D_
On Thursday Morning the tyre was inspected and did not shoe pressure loss so the car was driven home and made ready for collection by Hertz.
TITLE: Faulty Hertz Hire Car - Again

CASE_DESCRIPTION:
Whilst doing the Site Scaffold Inspections in our Kaefer Scaffold Yard today, Sunday the 7th of March, 2 x Doosan Operatives casually walked through our, barriered and controlled area._x000D_
When I approached them and asked the guys why were they were walking through our Storage Yard…. They replied that ‘they were just taking a casual walk around site and that they always go through there.’_x000D_
_x000D_
Now, we must please remember that we treat our Fully Operational, Storage Yard on site as a working Area. The same as we would treat a barriered off, signage present, working area on site._x000D_
The Forklift is constantly moving our material around in our Storage Area and at no uncertain terms should any contractor be entering our areas without consent from Kaefer Supervision or Yardman… Mick Cape_x000D_
This is for their own safety… this is the reason why there is signage on the gates. I did challenge the guys and explained the reasons why they shouldn’t be just walking through our controlled area. They took this on board and were approachable and understanding guys, however, alarm bells rang for me when they said… ‘they always go through there’_x000D_
_x000D_
I have also had a good chat with our Yardman and advised him to report this to the Kaefer Supervision or Andy Seddon, if this continues to happen._x000D_
I have had a good chat and highlighted it to Doosan Supervision/Management on site, however this may want to be reinforced by a Uniper Representative also?

This particular style of Sootblower (of which there are at least 8 on section 2 per unit) have a section of unguarded shaft on the side of the drive end.  The Operatives were in close proximity to the unguarded rotating shaft and were installing supports directly below it.  The operative immediately reported this to their supervisor and the working party withdrew from the area.

CASE_DESCRIPTION:
DMW Analyst was carrying out the routine personal dust monitoring on the Altrad stripping team when they noticed an amount of dust in the atmosphere inside the asbestos tent._x000D_
The pump was worn for a duration of 40 minutes at 2 litres per min. The limit of detection for this personal was 0.06 fibres per ml, the calculated result was 0.31 fibres per ml after a reading of 100.5 fibres on the slide in 33 fields. This is a fail by a large margin._x000D_
After speaking to the ALTRAD supervisors, they have informed me their limit of detection is 0.50 fibres per ml, so the result for them is not a fail, but they have acknowledged the reading is unsatisfactory, so a tool box talk will be conducted with Altrad staff._x000D_
A second personal test was run on the same operative which passed and was well below my limit of detection of 0.06 fibres per ml.
TITLE: Hazardous Substance Chemical/Material - exposure to carcinogens

CASE_DESCRIPTION:
Ein Fahrer der Spedition REAX meldete sich über die Freisprecheinrichtung der Liqvis LNG-Tankstelle in Freienbrink bei der ständig besetzten Stelle._x000D_
_x000D_
Der Fahrer hatte eine Undichtigkeit am LNG Tank seines VOLVO Lkw festgestellt, obwohl der Tankvorgang schon beendet und die Zapfpistole abgekoppelt war. Das LNG trat irgendwo unterhalb des Lkw-Tanks aus und lief auf den Boden, bzw. wurde über das Sicherheitsventil freigesetzt._x000D_
_x000D_
Die LNG-Tankstelle war zu diesem Zeitpunkt schon abgeschaltet, der Fahrer hatte bereits den NOT-AUS betätigt. Der Bereitschaftsdienst kam zur LNG-Tankstelle, führte eine Erstsicherung durch und prüfte die Gaskonzentrationen. Nach ca. einer halben Stunde lief kein LNG mehr aus dem Tank und es war nur noch eine minimale (unterer ppm-Bereich) bis keine Gaskonzentration feststellbar. Der LKW wurde daraufhin von der Tankstelle entfernt und der Fahrer informierte seine Einsatzzentrale bzw. den VOLVO-Kundendienst._x000D_
_x000D_
Die LNG-Tankstelle wurde wieder in Betrieb genommen, um den zweiten, dort noch wartenden Volvo-LKW der Spedition REAX betanken zu können. Nach Abschluss des Tankvorgangs an diesem VOLVO LKW trat das LNG dort auch wieder aus, so dass die Tankstelle erneut außer Betrieb genommen werden musste. Hier dauerte es ca. 1 Stunde bis kein LNG mehr auslief und der LKW vom Gelände der LNG-Tankstelle entfernt werden konnte._x000D_
_x000D_
Nach erneuter Inbetriebnahme wurde eine Betankung von 2 IVECO LKW durchgeführt. Hier kam es zu keinem LNG Austritt am Lkw-Tank nach der Betankung._x000D_
_x000D_
Der Einsatzleiter der Spedition REAX wurde kontaktiert und darauf verwiesen, dass bis zur Feststellung der Ursache für den LNG-Austritt durch den VOLVO-Kundendienst, keine Betankung der noch vor der Tankstelle stehenden, weiteren 2 Volvo-LKW von REAX durchgeführt werden kann._x000D_
_x000D_
Angeblich haben diese Fahrzeuge von REAX an den mobilen Anlagen in Hamburg und Stavenhagen (welche keine Liqvis-Anlagen sind) getankt und dort hatte VOLVO eine Ventileinstellung geändert._x000D_
Leider konnte weder der Spediteur noch die Fahrer vor Ort sagen, was dort gemacht wurde.
TITLE: LNG-Austritt am Lkw-Tank auf einer Liqvis-Tankstelle in Freienbrink

CASE_DESCRIPTION:
During an injection nomination at around 00:00, high pressure seen at pressure reduction valve (PRV) manifold (cavern pressure). On investigation no differential pressure was seen across the equalisation valve to the heat exchangers. Technician went to investigate and the equalisation gas bypass valve was open, despite showing closed on the plant control system (DCS). The valve was isolated at the time and then subsequently the limits were reset, during investigation at the time it appears to have lost it limits. Difficult to determine exactly why the limits were not correct as this occurred during the middle of the night. _x000D_
_x000D_
Believed a contributing factor could have been that the inlet separator valves may also have been passing and an increased pressure was observed at Inlet Separator 20 by the operator._x000D_
_x000D_
If the pressure had carried on increasing the plant would have tripped on high pressure.
TITLE: High pressure at pressure reduction valve manifold

CASE_DESCRIPTION:
The subject of LONE WORKING was brought to the attention of Carl Newcombe ( UNIPER ) by the Contractors (Phoenix) who had observed a UNIPER person lone working on an aspect of the HCL system which involved breaking into system within the confines of its Bund. 

I realise on initial review and discussion that:

•	He was wearing the correct PPE for the works.
•	Had a Safety Document issued by the SAP which had ensured safety from the system was in place, with WO and RAMS which apparently covered the work.
•	Person involved had a radio on the understanding that this was his means of communication with the Control Rm in the event of distress, injury or other problem.

Although all these points were in place on review of the RAMS; 

•	The RAMS generated by Eclipse on SAP did state No Lone Working at the very end of the Risk assessment.

What is the interpretation that should be followed when it states No Lone Working on the RAMS. 
My current thought is what passed without event on the day in question, next time might not and being reliant on a radio may not offer the timely response required.

CASE_DESCRIPTION:
Glycol Regeneration Unit 30 (GRU) tripped on Low Low Reboiler pressure when starting to process Rich Glycol. It appears QCA30AA101 Regen / Boil Off Gas Control Valve over shot when trying to balance the Reboiler pressure. On further investigation this follows similar trips on the 6th and 8th February._x000D_
_x000D_
This occurs as the Rich Triethylene Glycol (TEG) feed flow is increasing to close to the normal rate of around 6 m3/h. _x000D_
_x000D_
There is a spike in the reboiler pressure and in response the boil-off gas pressure control valve QCA30AA101 rapidly opens. This effectively controls the pressure rise which then rapidly reduces as the reboiler is vented through to the combustion chamber._x000D_
_x000D_
It would then appear that when a trips occurs QCA30AA101 cannot close quickly enough to maintain the reboiler pressure above the QCA30ZP005 low trip setpoint._x000D_
_x000D_
This trend pattern is common to all start ups but usually the pressure reduction is halted at around 30 mbarg. _x000D_
_x000D_
Worst case this could lead to air ingress into the reboiler from the combustion chamber creating a potentially flammable atmosphere.
TITLE: Glycol Regeneration Unit 30 Low Pressure Trip

CASE_DESCRIPTION:
There was a trip on GRU 20 caused by low cooling air pressure, < 10 mbarg on pressure transmitter QCA20ZP004 (HAZID 83)._x000D_
_x000D_
The cooling gas is delivered by fan (QCA20AM050) via a control valve (QCA20AA116) which controls the GRU 20 combustion chamber temperature at around 910 degrees._x000D_
_x000D_
For over an hour before the trip the pressure downstream of the fan started to decline and the control valve opened to maintain the cooling gas flow / combustion chamber temperature._x000D_
_x000D_
The fan delivery pressure will reduce as the control valve opens and the back pressure declines. However, when the control valve is 100% open (during the start up pre-purge) the pressure normally reads about 20 mbarg._x000D_
_x000D_
This suggests that the control valve opened in response to a reduced fan delivery pressure (to control the combustion chamber temperature) rather than being the immediate cause of it.
TITLE: SIS Activation HAZID 83 - GRU 20 cooling air low pressure trip

CASE_DESCRIPTION:
Contacted by NRW via phone with confirmation by email regarding complaint:

As discussed, at 13:30 on Friday 28th February NRW received an incident report from a member of public.

It states the following

Caller concerned about clouds of smoke/gas discharging from Connahs Quay power station noticed yesterday and is happening again today. Caller has tried contacting site direct, but the number given is not being answered. Caller says she doesn't want an excuse of "condensation", as she claims "condensation would evaporate, but these clouds are hanging about for 2 days".

Reply to NRW from Environmental Advisor:

Hello and many thanks for your email. 

We’re keen to ensure all environmental complaints / enquiries regarding the Power station are answered as quickly as possible. As you may be aware, last weekend (Feb 28th to March 2nd) has been a time of very low wind levels, bright sunshine, clear skies and generally cold atmospheric conditions. 

Shown below is a screen grab of the weather entry for Hawarden weather station for Feb 28th 2025

As a result we were called to run three CCGT Units for the majority of Friday and at times four units ran together over the weekend. 

I’ve checked with our operational staff and can state we were called to run three CCGT Units for the majority of Friday and at times four units ran together over the weekend,  on all these occasions the machines ran successfully, with no incident or issue and well within our emission monitoring limits as specified by the site’s Natural Resources Wales regulated Environmental Permit. As you may recall our Gas Treatment Plant closed in 2023 and is no longer operational. 

As a result, I can only conclude that the complainant is referring to the significant cooling tower plume which would be produced by active generational levels on a cold and crisp winter day. The uncommon environmental conditions are very likely to result in the large scale formation of such plume, made more visible by the cold clear winter skies. 

This emission of cooling tower vapour is permissible inline with current environmental legislation. Should you have the ability to contact the complainant then we would be interested to know which phone number was rung and failed to contact the power station. Clearly we’re keen to ensure there is always a clean means of communication in times of potential incident complaint and we can seek to correct any incorrect phone numbers which might exist anywhere. 

Please don’t hesitate to contact myself should you require any further information regarding this issue.
TITLE: NRW received an incident report from a member of public

CASE_DESCRIPTION:
At 09.49:33.913 GT Tripped due to humming event caused by low gas pressure from the PRS.  Low gas pressure recorded at the PRS due to ESD system operation closing the inlet ESD valve XV4002 and pressure reduction skid valve XV4480.
Scada system alarms showed ESD system operated due to PRS common hand switch operated, (PRS\ESD\UA4002) and ESD trip from CDC control room (PRS\ESD\HS4002C) receipt of this alarm would indicate that the operator himself had activated the PRS trip by pushing the emergency trip button in the plant MCR This cannot of been the cause of the PRS trip due to the operator not pressing the push button in the MCR, this was witnessed by gas operations as they were present in the control room when the ESD system tripped. whilst the gas pressure supply to CDC did fall the cause of the unit trip was from combustion instability (humming). it is recognised  that the low gas pressure would have tripped the GT by activation of the low gas pressure trip signals however on this occasion 'Humming' occurred operating the MAX 3 protection trip before the low gas pressure trip signals were received. The load at the time of the trip was 414MWgen (full load in 'OTC operation).
TITLE: GT Trip from PRS ESV’s closing

CASE_DESCRIPTION:
At 13.20 on Friday 18th February 2022 the integrity of Unit 7 Chimney Stack failed in high winds. The chimney stack collapsed and folded at a height of approx. 35-40m onto the corner of the HRSG roof, causing the top of the stack to collapse down the north side of the building in between Unit 7 and Unit 6.
Unit 7 GT Trip Push Button was initiated from the CCR at 13.21.
Unit was shut down as safely as possible with the GT & ST going On Barring. U61 was also shutdown in a controlled manner as a precaution, whilst U81 was already non operational due to Outage activities progressing.
A full site evacuation was ordered, with all site personnel and contractor workers being fully accounted for. There were no reported injuries or off site local impacts as a result of the collapse.

This incident occurred during storm Eunice, with a red weather warning Met Office alert having been issued earlier that day (having already been upgraded from an Amber alert issued the previous evening). Site had already implemented the high winds procedure which restricted any external work activities. This measure was agreed and communicated following the morning meeting performance dialogue. At approx. 12:00 hrs, as a further control measure all non essential works were ceased on site, with all contractor workers being stood down and returning to their respective office/messroom facilities.
TITLE: U7 Chimney Stack integrity failure (external RCA in progress - (EXTENDED 31/12/2022 Panel of Enquiry) 14/10

CASE_DESCRIPTION:
11 Oct 2022 Morning time : Enfield CCGT unit was on base load at appx. 390 MW

11;20 Duty shift operation technician during his second plant checks, noticed oil puddle in steam turbine basement ; On closer inspection also found oil spraying from Steam Turbine IP valve at North Side. 

Followed the leak to Turbine floor: Oil was found to be spraying from test pressure gauge on ST IP Stop Valve North Side.
 
Oil leak was immediately contained, REMIT declared & informed traders, Steam turbine controlled shutdown carried out, informed engineering and security gatehouse to prepare for evacuation & rollcall if required

Oil leak stopped once the steam turbine IP Stop Valve shut, Engineering team investigated, found test pressure gauge bourdon tube ruptured and oil leaking out from the damaged bourdon tube. Removed the pressure gauge, rectified oil leak 

Leak from hot surfaces and surrounding areas then cleaned, pipes lagging inspected and claddings cleaned from leaked & accumulated oil in lagging insulation,  

Gas turbine was kept ON during this time on bypass mode. Once the oil leak was rectified, REMIT declared and unit was brought back to base load.
TITLE: Steam Turbine IP Stop Valve  (North) Power oil leak

Being unable to enter the reduced MEL and UGC being unable to enter the MEL or reduce the PN for us, we incurred Significant Incidents from NGC for being 100Mw adrift of our PN and MEL. Eventually Siemens entered the MEL for us but not until 10:30hrs, with the EDL system down we had to receive telephone instructions for load drops to 350MW on Unit 1 and Unit 4, on EDL these will be seen as both units being 150Mw from their PN’s. CASE_DESCRIPTION: On run up this morning the steam turbine tripped at 44Hz due to low reheat steam temperature. Steam turbine had to slowed using the E shaft vac valve. On re run off the steam turbine program the step sequence faulted at step 18,This has led to believe to be the start up device. This is infact the steam turbine program looking for X5 which is lost, the Start up device appears to be a red herring. We found that even if the steam turbine is selected to fast from a trip it still looks for X5 positive which is not the same criteria of a HOF start. Hence the start up device is not the issue. Defects have been entered for the reheat thermocouples reading low.
TITLE: Steam Turbine Trip on Run up

CASE_DESCRIPTION:
02:15 Plant loading up from 3356MW BOA to 410MW PN
02:50 Prior to the event there was a rise in 18MAD20CY022 to 172um (which also happened on Sunday when there was a similar IP CV issue). This dropped right off once the plant load was stable
02:50 ST sequencer alarms received.
02:57 IP CV north started to open and close erratically.
Local observations were unable to prove that the valve was physically moving, however:
the IP drum level started to rise, 
the LP system pressure increased to alarm value, 
the plant load had become unstable,  
the IP CV south started to move in response to the IP CV norths position,
18MAB10CP001 pressure of steam IP inlet was unstable,

03:29 Called CH

CASE_DESCRIPTION:
U1 Boiler Recirc pump tripped/came out of service on Sat 07/03 @ 08:20 hrs with no abnormal alarms received, we were unable to restart the pump because when the pump was found out of service on a panel check, we were just outside of the 2.5hr window where we allowed restart it.
We have done some preliminary investigations and it appears the pump shut down around the time we were carrying out our routine weekend checks.
The particular checks in question involve us pressing the A & B side drum hydrastep level check alarm test buttons that are located on the Unit ESD panel, to confirm the alarm works.
We have carried out a controlled test and it appears that if both A & B side hydrasteps level buttons are tested at the same time, or in quick succession (both alarms up at the same time) this then takes the pump out of service on a drum low level (drum level low should trip the pump under normal conditions), however if the hydrasteps are tested one at a time then the pump remains in service. No alarms are received to indicate the recirc pump has tripped.
TITLE: Operational loss (not process safety) - U1 Boiler recirc pump tripped / came out of service

CASE_DESCRIPTION: On 1st August 2020 CO2 in the fire suppression tank warmed and increased in pressure sufficiently to lift the pressure safety valve at 25 Bar and -12OC. On investigation the cooling compressor and fan were found not running. Various electrical and mechanical checks were performed to identify the reason for the non-running cooling system, finally a reset button on the compressor control pressure switch rectified the fault and the CO2 began to cool again. At 16:00 on the same day a subsequent check found that although the pressure and temperature had dropped to -15OC and 22 Bar, ice formed under the safety valve seat during its lifting had caused the valve to not correctly seat and loose further CO2 to a mass of 7.2 tonnes. The minimum mass required to protect the unit during operation is 8.0 tonnes so the unit was broken down until a delivery could be arranged.
TITLE: U4 Fire Suppression CO2 Tank low level

CASE_DESCRIPTION:
During a routine water treatment plant stream regeneration it was found that acid had leaked from the system into the acid bund. The process was immediately stopped, and isolation valves closed. The acid within the bund was fuming off at this point making it difficult to approach the area, but estimations of level was about 3-4mm. Personnel withdraw from the area and opened exterior doors to provide some ventilation.
Email sent to all members of staff advising of the situation and asking them to cascade this to their direct reports and contractors.
After some discussion on the way forward and a Dynamic risk assessment had been carried out, an Operation Technician donned suitable PPE and respirator and re-entered the WTP room and pumped out the bund into the main sump. The bund was then washed down and pumped into the main sump, ready to be sent to the neutralisation tank.
The cause of the leak is suspected to be vent from the double block and bleed valve. There was no evidence of wet on the motor support plate or surrounding pipework.
TITLE: Acid leak in acid bund

CASE_DESCRIPTION:

Upon immediate investigation it was found that the flow to the cell of the instrument had been interrupted by "slime" but the constant head device was still flowing so there wasn't and alarm indicting loss of flow. 
On the night shift 11/09/19 when dosing again the same situation occurred and again dosing was stopped as soon as the alarm
initiated and the purge flow adjusted accordingly. 
The C & I team investigated as soon as they arrived on the following day shift to confirm that the cell had blocked again. Although this was not a breach of our permit there are still implications and reporting required.

CASE_DESCRIPTION:
On the 24/10 U3 was fired and steam to set occurred, it was showing high extraction pump conductivities >5uS before and after column. on the return to service unit 3 boiler chemistry deviated from target conditions. The extraction pump chemistry went into alarm state 3 (>1.0uS after column conductivity) during its on load run and the boiler water chemistry followed with the after column conductivity peaking at 51uS (alarm state 3). 
Due to the unit being ran to increase pressure for trevi testing there was no caustic dosing in the boiler water therefore no
boiler water protection. The pH of the feed flow and boiler water remained beneath the required level for the duration. LP dosing only occurred whilst the unit was generating. 
The boiler was dosed on the morning of 26/10 with a firing dose after discussions with a boiler team representative and the trevi continued after the dose had been added. The boiler was fired for 3hours after the trevi test was completed to facilitate blowdown and dosing of the boiler water. There was no steam sample available to assess the amount of sodium that has passed through the attemperator sprays into the superheaters. Both shells of the condenser had saw dust added to try and slow the ingress of contaminants and it was questioned if a condenser shell could be taken out of service to help to identify which shell the leak was in.
TITLE: Operational loss - U3 high extraction pump conductivities

CASE_DESCRIPTION: When units 1, 2 & 4 came on last week 10 out of 12 sample flows into the autolab were left isolated so there was only a limited view on the unit chemistry for unit 2 and none at all for units 1 and 4.

CASE_DESCRIPTION:
CDC module was at full load.
A large flame was witnessed on the control room CCTV coming from the west side of the top of the gas turbine.
A decision was made to manually trip the gas turbine from the control room  back panel emergency stop push button as simultaneously the fire alarm panel began to sound.
The above all proceeded within approximately 30 seconds of the flames being witnessed.
The site evacuation alarm was sounded along with a tannoy instruction to evacuate site.
The station MEL was redec'd to 0MW and remitted with energy trading.
The plant was observed as it was shutdown and the visible flames stopped on the tripping of the plant.  
The main gas valve 10EKG70AA001 was closed and gas vented to remove all gas from the building. The FGPH outlet valves were manually closed to 10EFG70AA001 passing.
Approximately 15 minutes after the GT being tripped a visual inspection was made of the GT which confirmed the dislodging of a flange thought to be that of the flame eye and lagging being emitted from the blow off pipework on the west side of the GT.
As there was no further risk to personnel the site evacuation was ended with the UMC remaining off limits and locked down.
Further inspection and repair planning commenced with the Engineering Team.
TITLE: Gas Turbine Combustion Chamber Flame Eye Failure.

CASE_DESCRIPTION: A recent Gas detection panel fault had closed the sites main Gas valve 10EKG70AA001 on protection. During the unit start up 3 attempts were made to start the GT for it’s DP run scheduled for 15:00 – 21:00. Each attempt failed due to time out of the fuel gas program as a result of 10EKG70AA001 not opening in time. On the 3rd start attempt, the valve was locally observed to see what was happening. It became apparent that the valve was trying to run open but not moving more than a fraction. Numerous attempts were made to drive the valve open, both electrically from the DCS, locally and manually using the handwheel. It was concluded the valve was either mechanically jammed or pressure locked. After some discussion, the decision was made to try and reduce the pressure upstream of the valve by venting off gas from the pre-heater. This was successful and allowed the valve to be re-opened.
TITLE: Main Gas Valve would not open.

CASE_DESCRIPTION:
At approximately 13.29 the G as panel in control room failed initiating a GT protection level 1 & 2 trip.
It was assumed that voltage fluctuations from the SFC had possibly caused a supply MCB to the panel to trip. (Running the SFC has been known to play havoc with some actuators on site, in particular ones associated with the aux boiler). Initial investigations revealed the power source for the gas panel (415v switchboard 10GMA06) had not tripped but further investigation within the gas panel were made which ascertained there was no 240v power to it’s internal power supply. A small fast blow anti surge fuse was found blown in the 240v supply line to the power supply unit. A new one was sourced and fitted. 240v power was now restored to the power supply unit, but there was no 27v DC output from the unit. Although the DC supply healthy light was lit on the front of the panel (from the back up batteries), there was no functionality from the gas panel at all.
Members of the Engineering team were called to site and the power supply unit was removed and dismantled to reveal it was badly burnt out inside. An alternative 24v DC power supply unit was obtained and temporarily installed which allowed the gas panel to be reinstated.
TITLE: Gas Detection Panel failure.

CASE_DESCRIPTION:
Gas turbine overspeeds, steam turbine overspeeds & steam turbine HP stop valve/governor valve tested successfully. Plant was stable and running at 400MW.
12:09hrs TST IP SV + CV Left FAIL 18MAB11EA121. Whereby, IP steam turbine governor valve closed fully, but the IP stop valve remained in intermediate mode (18MAB11AA001). Result was worsened vacuum >250mbar causing the steam turbine to trip (18MAX43EZ903_XU51). REMIT call submitted to Trading approximately 12:10hrs. Load dropped to SEL, drum levels controlled, air cooled condenser demin sprays put into service and sequencer selected to bypass. Grid were called to inform them of the situation.
By 12:17hrs, SEL was achieved. Due to standby to bypass being selected, gas turbine continued to deload.
At about 12:28hrs, Trading called requesting a REMIT update: 70MW from 12:30hrs to 13:30hrs. Then, between 13:30 and 13:43hrs increase load from 70 to 240MW. Remain at SEL until 15:00hrs.
Grid called and updated.
~ 13:34hrs programme device became disabled on the steam turbine and was manually given an ON command. Steam turbine became to ramp up from 70 to 240MW.
Steam turbine, at the time of writing is stable, and control valve stresses are improving (26 & 68% for HP and IP valves respectively.)
TITLE: Steam Turbine Trip, Following Trip Testing

CASE_DESCRIPTION: Whilst off load the MBFP tripped off barring and would not restart. The turbine proved to be tight and would not hand barr. The unit came off load at 23:00, MBFP on barring at 23:30. At 01:30 the bottom belt temperature suddenly dropped from 284 to 187 Oc , 5 minutes later the turbine tripped, no other operational activity was taking place at the time. The temperature continued to fall down to 95 Oc at 3:30 with the turbine still stationary. In an attempt to rectify the situation the condenser level was reduced and loop pipe drains opened. This increased the bottom belt temperature back up to 180 Oc at 05:00 and enabled the turbine to be hand barred half a turn. It appears a build up of condensate occurred within the bottom belt however investigations could not identify the cause of this . The turbine was shut down correctly, all drains checked in the correct position.

CASE_DESCRIPTION:
Valve 10EKT25AA101 FG P/HTR CIRC CTRL-V faulted with ‘Trouble Alarm’ and ‘Status Discrepancy Not Closed’. The valve had to be put in local operation at the Fuel Gas Pre-heater location and then manually operated in the open and closed  directions, the ‘fault re-set’ was then operated to clear the fault.  Multiple notifications under 21347109 are available to view valve fault history.  
During the valve fault the flow rate on the heating water side dropped and shut down the fuel gas preheater program.
 When the fuel gas preheater shuts down cooler natural gas flows to the GT burners. During this transition from Hot Gas to cooler gas the Gas turbine suffers combustion instability and combustion chamber rumble occurs causing GT Humming protection systems to operate.  
On the morning of 29-03-2021 the GT Humming protection operated as a direct result of cooler natural gas temperatures causing 0.2s to be added to the humming counter, there was a slight drop in load as the GT setpoint controller was switched off causing a slight imbalance during a load transient.
TITLE: Fuel Gas Pre-Heater shutdown / tripped causing GT Humming.

CASE_DESCRIPTION:

At 08.26 shortly after a Hydrant key had been collected for CW cleaning works, Jockey pump 2 cut in followed quickly by the electric fire pump.
It was assumed that the guys using the fire system on the CW  works had caused this.
When checking the A-site fire system @ ~09:30 the drain on the fire system manifold adjacent to block house 3a was found open.
This valve had not been open overnight and no permission had been given for the valve to be opened.
Taking into account the amount of water around the drain valve it is thought that it was opened at around the time the electric fire pump cut in.

CASE_DESCRIPTION:
At 16:40h the unit had a full load trip from 386MW/SO. ROMS was called at 16:51h. The unit was REMIT'ed out to 21:30h at 0MW. after investigation it was found that the trip was caused by aIP By-pass trip signal (10MAN51EZ001) which was instigated by a IP water injection flow protection (10MAN53EZ110). The IP by-pass spray water flow went below 0Kgs (-0.5kgs) on channels A and B, which has caused the unit trip. The IP by-pass was closed at the time and the IP Throttle valve was at 99% open. Paul Cockram and Will Hammond investigated the trip. A temporary simulation has been put in place whilst a Siemens recommend MOD is put in place.

Unit re-synchronised at 20:42 .
TITLE: CDC Full Load Trip

Work was immediately stopped and an attempt was made by the working party to extinguish using fire extinguishers  at the point of work. CASE_DESCRIPTION: Unit was on outage, with the open cycle CW pump in service,  at 11:48 control room operator heard a bang through the open window, and alarm  - Pres Beh open cy pum < 1.5 bar received.  Pump discharge pressure had been running at 2.9 bar but took a spike down to 0.5 bar, pump remained in service. ST forced cooling in progress, condenser vacuum and hotwell level remained constant. Outside operator observed water emanating from the ground and into the rain water pit and coming up through the drainage sump covers.  At the time is wasn't clear how fast water levels would rise and how much water there would be so the final discharge drainage pumps were left in service for 30 minutes until levels receded, before manually tripping.  water level has now soaked back into the ground but has left a sink hole by the drainage pumps

Upon closer inspection it was found that the rating on the side of the pressure switch was 12 bar or less.  The system it was fitted on runs at 120 bar.  The markings on the side of the pressure switch were very small and almost ineligible. After investigation it was found this indication was sensing pressure range and not max pressure. Switch was rated for system integrity wise.

CASE_DESCRIPTION: I had used the automatic pool car (volvo) for work at Connah's Quay. When I collected the car the previous week the rear drivers side tyre was appearing as low on the dashboard. I filled the tyre with air. Over the next few days the tyre went low again and I filled the tyre with air. On the 23rd of Jan it was clear that there was a leak in the tyre and i took it to Kwik fit who confirmed there was a puncture in the tyre. They also informed me the car was not fit to drive as the 2 front tyres needed to be replaced as they we not road worthy. The tyres were changed. over the next day the safety light came on for the one remaining tyre (rear passenger tyre)- I returned to Kwik fit who filled it with air and i reset the dash panel. over the rest of my stay the cars tyres remained safe.
TITLE: Pool car required 3 new tyres

CASE_DESCRIPTION: During welding works inside the Can sections for the new stack a welder was working using magnets to secure his welding blanket to the side walls of the can sections.
