CASE_DESCRIPTION:
During pressurisation of a delivery tanker of HCl to the WTP, a loss of fluid was observed from the foot valve area on the underside of the Brentag delivery tanker.  The tanker was immediately depressurised to reduce leak to a low flow. The fluid produced some gassing which was damped down using a fine spray from a washdown hose. The area was immediately barriered off to avoid unprotected persons entering the area. All forwarding systems for wash down residues was stopped and site surface drains closed. HVAC systems for adjacent buildings was stopped. Security informed to block access to site. Brentag driver requested assistance from Brentag emergency response team as per company procedure. Decision by Emergency Controller, in consultation with exec team, to ask site personnel to leave in a staggered approach to minimize risk of mass egress of 200+ staff (station on outage), rather than initiate sitewide evacuation. All persons confirmed off site by 15:03. External pump used to transfer product from tanker to designated delivery point. Leak flow decreased during transfer period and finished upon full transfer to tank. Tanker off site 17:30. Boiler Clean Drains Tank contents monitored and measuring 1.8pH. Advice sought from site chemist who approved use of Sodium Bicarbonate to neutralise contents of site chemically contaminated drains tanks. Tanks neutralised and monitored – in compliance with discharge permit. Discharged in purge.
No harm to persons or risk of as all control measures for delivery being followed as per approved operational procedure.
Full report to follow.
TITLE: HCl tanker leak developed in offloading point.

CASE_DESCRIPTION:
During the first Steam Turbine run up the cold re-heat NRV failed to open, on investigation it was found that the actuator and valve keyway had been assembled 90 degrees out.
The actuator, instead of releasing the valve plate to open on flow was trying to lift the valve plate open, this was held back by the steam pressure difference.
Under normal operation the actuator would remove the closing action and allow the plate to lift open when the pressure difference across the valve was sufficient.
In this state, had the actuator been powerful enough to force the NRV open, with positive DP down stream the flow would have reversed back to the HP turbine Exhaust.
TITLE:
Unit 7 Cold Reheat Assisted NRV re-assembled incorrectly.
29/09 LT - Extended for Emerson RCA 31/10/2023

CASE_DESCRIPTION: The mulsifyre detection air systems depressurised resulting in the operation of most of road 4 mulsifyre water systems and very nearly all of road 3 generator transformer associated fire systems, however operation of those systems was averted in this incident. The incident occurred following the release of and isolation of station general service air compressor no.2 which had been supplying the back-up alternative air supply to all three main station mulsifyre systems. The standby general service air system had not been started and this resulted in the GS air system and in turn the mulsifyre air detection system depressurising which caused the operation of road 4 mulsifye systems. The root cause of the incident being that the three individual mulsifyre detection air top up compressors are all unavailable through breakdown. The top-up compressors run excessively due to detection air system leakage. We have consequently been reliant on the alternative air provided by the GS air system to maintain pressure in the mulsifyre detection air systems, however this is not the primary purpose of the GS air system.
TITLE: PSNH - Station Mulsifyre Detection Air System

CASE_DESCRIPTION:
During a walk about it was noticed that diesel was visible on the floor around the temporary make up pump installation. Maintenance Delivery and operations team were informed of the leak and investigated. There had been a delivery of diesel that day and as no leaks were found at that time it was assumed there was a small spill of diesel from the delivery. 
On Thursday 28/09 it was noticed that even after cleaning up the diesel had returned to the roadway. On investigation and running of the diesel generator, a leak was spotted on one of the supply hoses inside the generator cover. The leak should have been contained in the bund, but a flange on the bund sump was found to be loose and the contents was leaking out of there. There was no indication that the diesel had reached the site drains, but a cover was put over the drain as a precaution and the spill cleaned up. The hose has been repaired and is not in a safe condition for use.

CASE_DESCRIPTION:
Statement from shift TL:
On arriving via Unit 4’s DA’s approach I noted one member of the scaffold team Vaping; I made note of him by sight and confirmed him by noting a sweet vape type smell on his breath during a brief chat with him; other’s in the team had minor PPE infringements, so  I decided to stop the job and speak to them all outside the boiler house where hearing protection isn’t mandatory. I requested the attendance of the Competent Person who was just entering the Boiler House as the working party descended the stairs (ie the CP  not being at the point of work but walking towards it.)
I confirmed that everybody had signed on the GSAF and reminded everyone of their obligations upon signing on. I went through the aspects of wearing the appropriate PPE and adhering to the mandatory standards.
I then challenged the individual who had been vaping and I had witnessed doing so. He denied the fact he been vaping at the 19 Metre level and was he hadn’t been contravening our site rules. 

With the CP, we agreed that the best thing was that the team should go back to the amenities as it was clear that the discussion wasn’t being open and honest. (19:40)

After discussions and many ample times for the individual to admit his breaking of site rules, I was left in a position whereby I could not trust him to work within the guidance and standards we set for ‘smoking and vaping’ in the designated areas safely on the site and additionally to the terms of  the GSAF. He became very agitated and confused, back tracking on his sequence of events.
With this in mind I requested that he should leave site for tonight, because not only did he chose to break our rules, but he had become confrontational to Kev and me during our discussions.
At 20:16 he left site and returned his fob to the gatehouse pending a discussion / investigation through Kaefer and CQ.
TITLE: Contractor found vaping @ 19m level of HRSG unit 3.

Potential to add a redundant card to allow auto-switchover in the vent of card failures.  Loop delivers self-check rather than SIF.

CASE_DESCRIPTION:
A repair request was raised with BP for EV charger number 2.  Syed Ishrat was given a name by BP for the person coming out to investigate.  The BP engineer was booked on site through VMS with Syed's contacts details as the host.

On arrival, he was booked in by security and directed to the power station.  Syed wasn't contacted by the gatehouse, so wasn't aware the engineer had arrived.

The engineer then went to the charger, reset it with the external reset button and was then spotted by myself as I went to my car.   No intrusive work other than pressing the reset button was carried out so the risk was minimal, but as a new person to site, the BP engineer would've been unaware of our safety and working practices.

I have found recently that I am rarely contacted by security when a visitor comes to site and the first that I hear of their arrival is when they arrive in reception and reception call me.  9 times out of 10 this isn't an issue, but if someone doesn't know to go straight to reception or is unfamiliar with site, they might end up somewhere they're not supposed to with no one site knowing that person is on site.
TITLE: BP Engineer unfamiliar with site and Uniper work practices allowed on site without host being contacted.

CASE_DESCRIPTION:
On Monday 22nd January at 08:40, I raised a request for a Hertz hire car which was accepted in 30 minutes. I received my confirmation and reservation booking: K7450329419. The delivery address was in Lincoln.
On Tuesday 23rd January at 08:32 I received a phone call from the branch in Nottingham, stating they could only offer me an electric car, would I be okay with this. I said yes and awaited the delivery of the vehicle later that day.
I then received a phone call from the branch stating the delivery drivers were having trouble charging the car, they were going to have to head back into Nottingham to charge the car and they would be an hour or so late delivering the vehicle to me, to which I said was okay.
By 9pm on Tuesday 23rd I decided that the hire car was not going to be delivered that night. I woke up on Wednesday 24th and called the branch at 08:00 when they opened to find out what had happened. As I was explaining the situation, I was rudely interrupted and told to stop talking as they knew who I was. I have now been informed, the delivery drivers continued to have issues trying to charge the vehicle and eventually had no option but to abandon the delivery as the car had no charge. They have vehicles being collected this morning and they will get one to me as soon as possible but that wont be until around 11:30am.
TITLE: Hire car not delivered on time

CASE_DESCRIPTION: Whilst dealing with an analyser problem in the WTP it was noticed that there was water spraying from somewhere approximately 3 metres above ground level.  Further investigation identified that it was from the dosing pipework for effluent system 2 which was in service and in the process of neutralising the effluent tank.  I immediately went to local control room and stopped effluent system 2 and made it unavailable. The leak was from plastic pipework that travels over the top from the pumps to the ejector skid.  This pipework fails regularly as a result of movement when the pumps stop/start or a dose of either caustic or HCL is applied.  At the time of the leak the PH of the tank was 13 so it was dosing with HCL.  The leak would have been a mixture of HCL and motive water.  The area is always barriered off due to the regular failings off the plastic pipework used on this system. Notification raised for repair to be carried out.  Improvements to the plastic pipework need to be made as this is a regular occurrence.
TITLE: Water treatment plant  - Failure of effluent dosing pipework

CASE_DESCRIPTION:
Concerns around lift functionality and safety.

Incident:
I used the lift on Saturday 15th July approx 09:45.  I pressed floor 3. The inner doors seemed to jolt before it started moving.  I opened the inner door (believing that the lift had stopped and I was at the desired floor - landing arrival alarm has been disabled!) to find the lift had not fully travelled to the correct floor.  It opened with very little resistance and opened enough to stop the lift dead and put it into fault mode. CASE_DESCRIPTION:
While carrying out fault investigation under MO - 1180967658 an unexpected operation of the BFA to BFB interconnector caused loss of power to the BFB board.

Breaker 61BFT20GT200 (BFB feeder) was placed in test position for the purposes of fault investigation.

Upon reaching step 5 of the MO "Operate breaker locally and observe operation." a peer check was carried out to ensure that the correct operation was being undertaken.

Once the ON(Test) button was depressed, breaker 61BFT20GT200 (BFB feeder) closed, this was the intended outcome. However with this, 61BFA15GS021 BFA to BFB interconnector opened, this caused loss of power on the BFB board. This caused condensate extract pump 2 to trip, fortunately pump 1 was available and swapped over without issue. Other systems impacted were as follows, MBH55 GT exhaust cooling fan, CMAS fan 2, vacuum breaker etc. The event list is attached.

In normal operation if the the BFA feeder was closed and the BFB feeder was to close the interconnector should open. However the collective understanding was that in the test position this logic would be void. 

Upon investigation of the logic it was found that this is not the case.
TITLE: Loss of power to U6 BFB board causing trip of condensate extract pump and other systems fed off BFB board.

CASE_DESCRIPTION:
From Enerlytics alert dated 22/03/2023 @ 14:38
During routine OLVMS monitoring, UTG noticed higher than normal levels of vibration along the ST shaft line during the run up on 16th March. The highest levels were seen on the IP/LP Eccentricities where levels peaked at 290 um pk-pk with the unit at 842 rpm, during a normal run up a typical amplitude at this speed would be 25-50 um pk-pk. The change in vibration was 1/rev driven suggesting the unit had run up with a temporary bend.

A review of the barring file prior to this run up shows that the turbine remained stationary for approximately 1 hour following the previous run down on the evening of 15th March. The barring file shows the rotor straightening across the barring period, however the elevated vibration levels had not fully subsided before the start of the run up. If the unit was had remained on barring for a few more hours the rotor may had been able to fully straighten prior to starting.

Once the machine reached full speed and was loaded up, the vibration levels subsided as the machine straighten. Subsequent run ups and run downs have passed by without incident, comparing well to previous and giving no cause for concern.
TITLE: Unit 6 Steam Turbine High Vibrations on Run-Up.

CASE_DESCRIPTION:
Re-power project Trant Engineering additional work scope on behalf of EDF to remove old transformer bunds BHT03 and BHT05 waste.
EDF via email 24/03/2023 issued waste collection note to Uniper project team as documentary evidence to be added to project handover documentation of which was in addition to Hitachi (main contractor work scope).
On review of information project team had a meeting on the 04/04/2023 CDC Environmental officer to determine that project teams understanding was correct, the process had not been followed and that the documentation was non compliant for the reasons given below prior to issuing response to EDF.

Waste collection note issued is non-compliant for the following reasons: 
•	The collection and delivery addresses are to be in full including post codes
•	SIC code 3511 is missing
•	Producer (Uniper) has not signed the document and the declaration which has been ticked should be a declaration for the producer (Uniper) to sign (Appears that waste has been removed from CDC site without signed authorisation from Uniper representative as per agreed process).
•	Tonnage is not acceptable as 1 load as there are 2 EWC codes 17.01.01 and 17.05.04 in which Uniper require separate tonnage per code 

In addition Uniper have checked the waste carrier license 401 5100 30 and confirm license is still valid. Prior to waste being removed from Uniper CDC site Uniper should of received completed waste classification forms (WM3 assessments) for the 2 different wastes. As the EWC codes are mirror codes and have been deemed as non-hazardous by Trant Uniper require analysis data i.e. copy of test results to demonstrate non-hazardous waste. This information should have been provided to Uniper for review and acceptance prior to any waste being removed from site as per agreed process, this does not appear to have happened and a synergi case has been raised.

Response sent to EDF 04/04/2023 to provide the correct documentation and carry out an investigation with Trant Engineering and to provide an update to enable Uniper to complete the investigation.
TITLE: Removal of Waste from CDC site non-compliance

CASE_DESCRIPTION:
This Synergi has been raised on behalf of EDF by Asset Support & Outage Excellence UK 

Decommissioning of the CDC MUW supply pipework to include removal of the pipework, 10-PAR-20-CF001 flow meter and 10-PAR-20-AA151 Actuated Control valve.

Prior to the Safety document being written the SAP and the Uniper Project Engineer visited the point of work to discuss the exact works. The SAP had opened the drain valve on the redundant  MUW pipework and air could be heard rushing in there was no water from the drain proving the isolation of 10-PAS-72-AA002 of which separated the new MUW system form the old MUW system thus proving the integrity of the valve. A further discussion between the SAP and Uniper Project Engineer took place reference the status of the MUW pump booster station reference the HV cable disconnection and that he MUW booster pumps could not run as there was no power present.

A Safety document was issued by the Uniper SAP for the decommissioning works to proceed and at approximately 12:30 p.m., the Uniper Project Engineer received a phone call from Trant Works Manager responsible for the works to ask if an isolation had been applied at the EDF end of the MUW supply pipe to CDC.

An email was received at  12:37 from EDF Site Separation Lead Mechanical Engineer Decommissioning as follows:

I have just been to see the Trant guys doing the make up decommissioning work on CDC, I did a spot check on the safety document, and subsequently asked Nathan Pearson to stop works.
 
The only mechanical isolation in place is on valve 10-PAS-72-AA002, this valve separates the old system from the new system.
It appears no valves have been isolated upstream from the booster station end.
 
If EDF were to start one of it’s make up pumps, this could potentially feed water all the way to the CDC site, either causing harm when flanges are split, or flooding the CDC
 
Nathan is going to speak to Steve Nelson and the Ops team, could you please raise a Uniper synergy case for this.
 
The booster station may be electrically disconnected, but there is nothing to stop valves from being opened
TITLE: Make-Up Water Redundant Pipe Removal

CASE_DESCRIPTION:
A near hit incident occurred involving a forklift and a stack of heavy steel plates. The incident took place at outside Unit 1 turbine hall at approximately 14:05

Details of the Incident:

Forklift Operator:  PES 
Equipment Involved, Steel Plates

Sequence of Events:
The forklift was transporting a stack of heavy steel plates.
As the forklift took a corner, the plates began to slide off the forks.
The sliding plates posed a significant risk of falling and potentially causing injury or damage.

Immediate Actions Taken:
The forklift operator immediately stopped the vehicle to prevent further movement of the plates.
The area was cordoned off to ensure safety until the situation was stabilized.
Additional personnel were called to assist in safely repositioning the plates.

Root Cause Analysis:
Load Securing: It was identified that the steel plates were not adequately secured before transport.
Forklift Speed: The speed at which the corner was taken may have contributed to the instability of the load.
Corner Handling: The angle and method of turning the corner were reviewed for safety compliance.
TITLE: U1 OUTAGE - FLT Transporting Generator Casing Steel Plate

CASE_DESCRIPTION:
During routine testing of the liquid level still chamber.
The “Control” level transmitter was found to have values entered the upper and lower ranges, that were different to the identical safety transmitter and identical control level transmitters on the two other identical vessels. 

It was also observed that the amplitude of the waveform seemed to be significantly lower than on the same device at other positions. 

The still well was filled with water and the level increase – immediately an issue with the “0” position was obvious the water level continued to be increased and no response was given from the transmitter.

The correct parameters were entered, and the waveform threshold retuned. 
The liquid level test then recommenced. 
The transmitter performed as expected at 
0 ,25,50,75,100% points. 

As the still well drained, the Transmitter registered the 75% point, however after that the reading froze despite the still chamber being totally empty. 

Should this have happened in normal operation the control valve could have opened despite the liquid level not being present.

CASE_DESCRIPTION:
During the morning of the return of U1 from main outage, it was noted that superheat spray flow was not sufficient as load increased.  The duty AUO was despatched to investigate the issue, helped by the commissioning lead operator.  They found the spray pump hand isolating valves in the closed position.  The valves could not have been 100% closed as there was sufficient flow to achieve ~5kg/sec of flow at the sprays.

These valves are very large hand isolating valves that are not routinely operated (2 man job to open / close) and are not part of any outage isolations as they are left available for maintenance during the outage.  

The work lists from the PFW's show that the valves were worked on during the outage, and we suspect they were operated by the maintenance team to prove operation following maintenance, and hence left in the closed position.

The valves should have been picked up as closed during the initial commissioning phase, and then again on the pre start checks prior to RTS of the pump.

This is the first Main outage RTS since the change to the outage procedure of filling the DA with FFA and forward filling of the feed system with the SSFP's.  With the introduction of the new boiler filling dosing skid, it means we no longer carry out the above step.  Instead we hold the feed water at the HP heater outlets and then fill the boiler using the filling pump with pre dosed water.  Then during the boiler Hydraulic, we back fill the steam circuits through the spray bypass line.  This meant that during our commissioning phase the Spray pump system got missed and highlighted a gap in the new procedure.

The pre start checks were carried out by the duty AUO.  On interviewing the AUO he stated that he had carried out a pre-start check, but only checked the electric valves as per usual for a normal return from a 2-shift.  This was a relatively inexperienced AUO who had never seen the hand isolators operated before.
TITLE: U1 Return to service from Outage - Spray pump hand isolating valves found in incorrect position.

CASE_DESCRIPTION:
U1 A SSFP was being prepared for RTS ready for a test run, followed by pressure testing of HP heaters.

The SSFP was de-isolated & pre start checked by the commissioning operator.  The oil pump was put into service and the oil system checked for correct pressures, and checked over for leaks.  No leaks were observed following the oil pump going into service.  The Operator then walked the HP feed system to ensure a route was available for the SSFP's and de-isolated the remaining plant.  The Operator called the Authorised Person over the radio to make the HV breaker available for service.  As the AP was heading to the switchroom the Operator returned to the pump ready for the start; a period of approx 30 mins had passed.   On returning to the pump he observed a large pool of oil under the A SSFP oil filters.  On closer inspection the vent on the filter was found to be slightly open with a stream of oil running from it.  The filter vent was closed immediately to stop the flow.   The AP was called on the radio to divert straight to the pump.  Dresser Dry was deployed to dam the oil and to prevent entry to any turbine hall drains.   There is a 3" hole in the turbine hall floor adjacent to the A SSFP, and some of the oil had flowed down the hole which leads directly to the sub- basement.  Dresser dry was deployed in the sub-basement around the oil & the spill contained.

The oil mop in the reject tunnel was immediately put into service as a precautionary measure.  There was a very slight film of oil on the water before the weir, but nothing observed after the weir, or at either the station drains sump or Ash Fines Pit.

The filter vent is not operated as part of the RTS procedure,  and is only used to prove the filter off pressure during a filter change.  I suspect that at some point during U1 outage the vent cock handle has been knocked slightly, causing the vent to pass when the oil pump went into service which was missed on the initial inspection.
TITLE: U1 A SSFP Oil Filter vent valve found slightly open.

CASE_DESCRIPTION:
Unit 6 HP Bypass Water Injection Control Valve logic was requested to be changed to match Unit 7's, that has been on trial. 
The logic is designed in such a way there is a test facility (a switch to turn the modified logic on/off). This was in place so that the logic could be switched on when DCS engineers where on site, during a run up, to monitor it and tune it if required. 
With the test bit off, the new logic would not be active and the control would not be changed. 
The logic was copied, but an error was made and the test facility was accidently left on. During Unit 6's run up after its outage, the spray valve wasn't operating. This is when the 'test' logic was still realised to be on. The test facility was turned off and that allowed the spray to function, stopping the unit from tripping on high temperatures.
TITLE: Unit 6 HP Bypass Water Injection Control Valve logic modification fault.

The switchroom was ventilated and checks of adjacent areas of the switchroom annex confirmed that the source of the smoke was from the Inverter Room. As the smoke cleared, on inspection none of the equipment in the associated switchroom appeared to be in distress! With the support of the electrical team each panel was inspected and it was believed that EML4 lighting inverter was the most likely source although it was still operating apparently normally.
TITLE: PSO - Main Control Block Fire Alarm

CASE_DESCRIPTION:
While completing fuel gas stream A underperformance investigation and rectification, it was discovered that the fuel gas heater failed to trip when the transmitter is placed in open loop. 

This means that any failure of this nature would not be detected and the control room has no visibility  of the transmitter. Therefore, if the control transmitters (EKC20ZT006 or EKC20ZT008) were to open circuit it would drive the heaters to 100% output!
(The control and trip transmitters utilise the same cabling so have a massive common cause failure).

This could lead to disabling of the protection layer, as the control system drives energy into the heaters.
TITLE: Failed Trip Test on control Transmitters of Fuel Gas Heater Stream A

CASE_DESCRIPTION:

The Gatehouse radio was left in the Gatehouse and set to ‘Man Down On’ and thus activated an alert on the Gatehouse, CDC & KPS Control Room radio base stations.
Operations personnel in the CDC Control Room attempted to contact the security guard on the radio & site security mobile phone, to no avail.
Fortunately, operations personnel in the CDC Control Room were able to spot the security guard walking around site, which negated the need to escalate the matter. Operations personnel in the CDC Control Room were able to speak to the security guard on his return to the Gatehouse and instigated additional contact protocols to ensure there were no repeat occurrences that night.
The following morning, upon his arrival to site, the day security guard reset the Gatehouse radio base station which was still in alarm. The night security guard simply turned off the Gatehouse radio and turned down the volume on the Gatehouse radio base station to silence the audible alert, as he did not know how to reset it.

On the evening of 22nd July 2024, the same security guard once again set off the ‘Man Down’ radio alert and was given instruction on how to reset it by Killingholme operations personnel. However, at the start of the morning shift on 23rd July 2024, Killingholme operations personnel found the KPS Control Room radio base station in alert, so it would appear the security guard had triggered the alert again at some point during the night.

These are serious matters of concern, which highlight the security guard’s lack of understanding and discipline, repeatedly creating unnecessary work for numerous Uniper personnel.
TITLE: Misuse of 'Man Down' feature on Site Radios

CASE_DESCRIPTION:
Forklift Operator: PES

The forklift was transporting a stack of heavy steel plates from the turbine hall on U1.

Load Securing: It was identified that the steel plates were not adequately secured before transport.

CASE_DESCRIPTION:
When taking U6 off load the HP bypass spray wasn't controlling properly causing high after bypass temperatures and tripping the HP Bypass.This is a known issue so we were expecting this to happen. Due to the Bypass trip the HP header pressure rises as the steam has nowhere to go. When the bypass was reset it was noticed that the process value on the HP bypass was struggling to meet the set point and was lagging behind quite a bit. This caused the HP header to rise significantly and the safety valves lifted. At this point the unit was off load but it was noticed that the GT EV burners were still lit adding to the high steam pressure situation. We tried to put an 'OFF' on the GT sequencer but this didn't work so we used the emergency trip button located on the unit desk. Once the flames were out the pressure started to subside but the HP bypass was still clearly not controlling as it should.Due to the significance off the HP bypass the unit was MEL'd to 0MW until 12:00 01/10/24
There are x3 issues here:
1. HP Bypass spray water control not controlling well enough to stop the HP Bypass tripping on high temperatures
2. Hp Bypass process value not following the set point as it should.
3. The GT not shutting down correctly and taking the flames out when the Circuit breaker was opened.
TITLE: U6 HP Bypass failed to operate correctly and boiler safety valves operated

CASE_DESCRIPTION: Engineering investigated a report from operations regarding BHC switchboard voltage monitoring reading 0V. Upon investigation, it was found that out of the three inline fuses feeding the switchboard monitoring equipment (one fuse per phase), two of the three had blown. It was also noted that the fuse ratings were incorrect and mismatched (2A on L1 phase, 4A on L2, and 16A on L3). The 16A fuse was still intact. The datasheet for the monitoring equipment specifies a maximum ampacity of 3A, suggesting that the 16A fuse was significantly over-rated, and this is likely why it did not blow at the same time as the other two fuses. Incorrect fuse ratings can lead to damage of downstream equipment and poses a potential fire risk in the event of an overcurrent fault.
TITLE: BHC Incomer Monitoring Incorrect Fuse Ratings

CASE_DESCRIPTION:
The following is an example of detail found on an MO and is an example that should never be allowed to happen: -_x000D_
_x000D_
"While going through the plan today I noticed the above MO number already had a SAP decision on it, looking in enhancement it also had a Permit assigned to it – 2020/00406. _x000D_
_x000D_
As it looked like an older number I checked nisoft and this permit was “Not Issued” on 15/05/2020. _x000D_
_x000D_
I am concerned that we have received a MO on the plan that already has a safety decision applied along with a permit that is not ‘live’. I think the possibility of being able to re-using old MO’s needs investigating. I thought this was not possible. If it is then this has potentially serious consequences._x000D_
_x000D_
In this case the system has stopped any potential accidents as the MO could not be used with a cancelled/not issued document, however, If the original safety decision was at lower level such as a FWI and that MO was regurgitated but the plant/apparatus condition has since changed (therefore requiring precautions) it could prove to be more serious. As SAP’s we do not and can not check through every SAP decision that has already been made, some don’t even see this as they use GWOZ and only look at MO’s on the plan that are set to SRDR."_x000D_
_x000D_
Questions I feel need answering are:_x000D_
1. Who is capturing the volume of gaps in the standard of MO as there is no log book or day SAP in position._x000D_
2. What was captured in previous audits, regarding SAP MO's and documents, were any actions identified and carried out?_x000D_
3. Discussion surrounding who and when a Safety Decision should be made to a MO and when is it suitable to place a document in 'mod' is being held across members of the Ops Team - should there be clarity from the management team so there is consistency?
TITLE: Review management of work system between Ops and Engineering and between the 5 Ops Shift Teams, with the aim of achieving consistency across the shift teams when assessing MO's and preparation of documents. CASE_DESCRIPTION:
Unit BOAI’d to service, there was no PN for the entire period….

Unit tripped shortly after start-up on 30th due to low HP feed flow. Feed reg bypass valve faulted. Fault rectified but not in time to save unit from protection trip.

Mel Redeclared to 0MWso @ 12:50hrs 
MEL Redeclared available (sloping MEL to reflect run up) from 14:00hrs 

HP Feed Reg Bypass valve faulted causing HP Feed low flow protection, operator managed to regain flow and re-set GT emergency shutdown, the situation repeated itself and the operator was unable to re-set the GT protection shutdown before unit de-synchronised.

CASE_DESCRIPTION:
Kue a sub contractor to Doosan undertook grit blast of the primary and secondary platens in U4 boiler. Agreed method was to sweep and bag waste and transport to 'duct bags' on pallets to be segregated on site, this was part of method statement and confirmed again just prior to work. Work was undertaken from Friday 20/5/22 to Sunday 22/5/22. Altrad provided resource to collect the waste on pallets and to remove and store onsite. The work area was inspected at the end of the job, the main focus was the prep, however it was noted that the scaffold was clean, free of waste grit and the when asked if the plastic sheeting had been removed we were told "yes" Kue also made a point to say that the Altrad resource had been very helpful, as the Altrad resource had been set up specifically to remove the waste it was assumed that this therefore had gone well. Based on inspection of the work area, the Kue paper work was signed by Chris Onions, both for completion of the shot blast areas and that the work area was clean and tidy. Kue left site on Sunday 22/5/22.  

On Monday 23/5/22 the Environmental team enquired where the waste was stored as it could not be found. On enquiring with the Altrad resource, they confirmed that there had been no waste generated. It was at this point that it was realised that Kue had not followed the agreed method for waste removal and had undertaken a different method. On inspection of the ash hopper it became apparent that it contained the waste shot.

An enquiry with Kue via Doosan, it was confirmed that not waste was collected and bagged, it instead was swept off the sheeted scaffold directly into the ash hopper. No waste had left site, no waste had entered any other skip/bin and the total amount of waste was 4 tonnes. The waste is therefore contained in the ash hopper and will be removed by shovel and bag and disposed of as per original plan.
TITLE: U4 Kue grit blast waste, failure to segregate waste as per agreed method resulting in additional work to properly segregate waste.

CASE_DESCRIPTION: Following submission of the 2020 verified Annual Emissions Report on 23rd March 2021 to the Environment Agency, an error was identified on the report. The error relates to the permitted fuel, F7 Gas Oil.  Activity data is taken from the turbine flow measurement system (GO FM1 and FM2) recording gas oil consumption to each gas turbine. The units of measure are recorded  in gallons, gallons are then subsequently converted to litres and finally converted to tonnes.  For the 2020 annual submission on 23rd March 2021 the  conversion factor of 4.54609 from gallons to litres was omitted from the calculation.  This resulted in an un-intentional under report of 664.04 tonnes of CO2.
TITLE: Ratcliffe 2020 EU ETS Gas Turbine Oil CO2 error

CASE_DESCRIPTION: After suffering a GT trip during the start at 05:30 (separate synergie entered for this) the unit synchronised at 07:30. During the hold period it became evident that the Steam Turbine X5 criteria would not be achieved for a number of hours. GT load was held back at 60MW which is unusual as this load should be around the 90MW mark. GT exhaust temperature was 465 degrees C which seemed low for the required HP steam temperature to clear X5. Theory that some HOF settings may be interring with run up, so a decision was made to shut the unit down and start again. Second attempt HP bypass appeared to behave as expected i.e. in flow control vs pressure control on previous attempt and X5 criteria was clearing at a more accelerated rate. GT load was held the same causing a prolonged hold period of 1hr 10mins vs 40mins expected. Looking back at previous starts the GT load is being pegged back at 60MW vs 90MW expected.
TITLE: Commercial loss due delayed start.

CASE_DESCRIPTION:
The turbine waste oil tank high level alarm initiated at approx 1500hrs. The AUO was dispatched to check the level in the tank and he confirmed that the level was high but no chance of overflowing.
Considered transferring oil over the waste oil purification tank, however this tank was already full. 
Contacted Altrad to inform and check whether they were aware that the tank was full and needed emptying. Person responsible had left site but message was left for the following morning.
The wider shift team conducted further checks of the waste oil recovery tank systems to confirm that there was nothing draining such as oil cooler / coalescers etc. Nothing concerning was found across the four units.
At approx. 1930hrs it was observed that the turbine waste oil tank was overflowing.
Immediate action was taken to contain the oil within the local area and prevent ingress into the drains.
Altrad Boiler Ops were contacted to provide support with cleaning and responded quickly with a gulper. The oil spill and spill-dri was cleared.
The source of the problem was identified as a steam / water leak on  Unit 4 spray water booster pump which was causing the turbine waste oil tank to fill with water. This was balancing into the MBFP waste oil recovery tank, which in turn was being pumped into the turbine waste oil tank.
The unit 4 turbine waste oil tank was in a barriered area (associated with the leak causing the problem) and was consequently not checked as part of the operational check associated with the high level.
The turbine waste oil tank was covered with a tarpaulin to prevent further water ingress.
The site services team were contacted to arrange further support to assist the night shift with the follow up cleaning and lowering of the waste oil tank level below the high level alarm and monitoring / gulping of the main reject tunnel station water drainage of any carry over oil which was completed.
TITLE: Main turbine hall waste oil tank

CASE_DESCRIPTION:
During the Fall Arrest inspection yesterday, Integral delivered a new harness for inspection, which failed. The Inspector noted that some of the catches were the wrong way round and while this isn’t a failing in itself it would make the harness uncomfortable to wear, as the catches would rub on the chest of anyone wearing it. 
As this was a new harness the Inspector added it to the system and then did a thorough check of all the details provided on the label. He found that the harness was manufactured in India in 2024, but only showed a CE safety marking, which is no longer valid for new items in the UK since 2023. This means that the harness is illegal as there’s no proof it has been tested to the correct UK CA standard. 
Inquires were made about where the harness was purchased from and no records have been found so far.
When I spoke to Facilities later they didn’t remember ordering a harness for Integral, and were going to investigate.
Facilities don't keep their own inspection register.
TITLE: Harness/fall arrest inspection by British Engineering Services - Harness found with the wrong safety markings

CASE_DESCRIPTION:
On the 28th February noticed puffs of black smoke being emitted from GRU 30 stack, not long after the Rich TEG feed had been introduced and on the following day the unit tripped on low reboiler pressure, again as the Rich TEG feed was being established._x000D_
_x000D_
The PI trend for the low pressure trip on the 1st March follows a very similar pattern to the trips observed in February & March 2020 and at the time wetter than normal Rich TEG was put forward as a possible explanation for a large spike in the reboiler pressure. However, the upstream GDU moisture analyser EKC10CQ001 wasn’t operating at the time which made this quite speculative._x000D_
_x000D_
One possible explanation for this could be the residual wetter than normal TEG held up in the contactors (approximately 14 m3) which would be transferred to the Rich Buffer tank in the subsequent withdrawals during which time it would be made partially drier by the incoming TEG although this would still have quite a high moisture content._x000D_
_x000D_
While the wet TEG theory remains far from conclusive it now has more credibility and GRU 30 was operated on the 2nd March with a Rich TEG feed which probably contained a more normal moisture content and no operating issues were observed.
TITLE: GRU 30 incomplete combustion event and reboiler low pressure trip

CASE_DESCRIPTION:
@ Approx 07:30 Sunday morning 04/12/22, a fuel oil leak was discovered on Unit 1 Burner Front.  The source of the leak was C16 oil burner inlet hose which had developed a leak.  The leak appears to be at the rear of the hose where it was touching the steel work.   The spray from the Leak was localised to C16 / C17 burner, but the excess has tracked down the pipework and steel work to the boiler basement.

It is unclear at what time the leak developed, but was not identified by the end of Saturday Day shift when the burner front was checked at approx 15:00hrs. 
The fuel oil had ran down the lower levels of the burner front, into the snake pit and Into the boiler basement adjacent 'C' pa fan.   As soon as the leak was discovered, the drain between 'C' PA fan and the ash hopper was plugged, and dresser dry applied to the immediate area.  Dresser dry was then applied to the higher levels where ever the oil had pooled.  Air heater wash sump, ash fines pits and ash crusher pits have showed no signs of oil as of 09:30 04/12/22.
TITLE: PSNH - U1 C16 Oil Burner hose leak

CASE_DESCRIPTION:
On unit 3 run-up A1 Re-heater Intercept valve tripped and went undetected. The unit was synchronised and proceeded to load up, at approx. 440MW Hot Re-heater safety valve 166 lifted as a result of the intercept valve being tripped. Although the HP exhaust pressure was only 40 bar, indicating the safety valve had lifted “light” (there are also 4 other R/htr safety valves passing on this unit)._x000D_
The unit load was reduced to 230MW initially thus reducing R/htr pressure and enable a gag to be installed, unsuccessful the load had to be reduced further to 20MW allowing successful fitting of the gag. Unit load was then returned back to full capacity. _x000D_
The problem of the tripping intercept valves on fast (5 minute) run-ups has been highlighted several times in the past and a previous OIT raised. Also, the turbine valve tripping isn’t highlighted significantly enough, meaning operators can miss this crucial problem.
TITLE: PSNH  - U3 re-heater Intercept valve tripping leading to r/htr safety valve 166 to lift.

CASE_DESCRIPTION:

The mulsifyre system was still live and the loss of supplies to the store included loss to the mulsifyre compressor which primes the air sensing lines.  When the pressure in the lines dropped the fire system was discharged in the oil storage area.  This deluge caused damage to several boxes of grease cartridges and also allowed oil drip trays to overflow.  The contents of which went down the station drains.

Oily water also proceeded to pass through to the office area and into the switchroom and down a cable tunnel.

This was not discovered properly until Tuesday 18th Feb as the Altrad oil supervisor was working in the main stores on Monday 17th Feb and didn't go in to the oil stores.  Legacy issues with the fire alarm system prevented the Operation teams from identifying where the mulsifyre system had been discharged and led them to believe there was a significant leak.
TITLE: Oil store flooding due to Mulsifyre system discharge

Lack of barriers demarcating the work area, no safety A frame or harness in place, no second man above ground, gas monitor not being worn and 4 inches of water in the draw pit.
Trant Engineering 755-TEL-XX-XX-PL-Z-0009 – Emergency Response Plan not being adhered to.
Trant Engineering 755-TEL-XX-XX-MS-C-0057 Rescue Plan not being adhered to.

IP steam system Safety Valves lifted. (ST out of service, HP bypass valve Open)._x000D_
At the DCS the IP bypass system spray water Valve recorded 90% Open but with little or no flow. _x000D_
At -3MW Generated Load a GT Trip was initiated from the Unit Desk._x000D_
The IP Safety Valves closed almost immediately._x000D_
On investigation it was determined the Condenser neck temperature had recorded a >Max 2 Temperature, which had deactivated the IP Bypass Function Group. At the IP bypass system spraywater Valve, the valve / positioner linkage was found not set correctly, the linkage cone was not in the correct position. The positioner output was asking for 90% but the valve was physically shut. The linkage cone was refitted, the valve was stroked from the CCR to confirm correct operation._x000D_
A notification was raised to check valve positioner linkage at next opportunity.
TITLE: U6 IP Bypass system Safety Valves Lifting

Up until 2014 site had a problem in the Winter with the wellheads tripping on low temperature when the wellhead flow control valve was closed, usually when the DCS Stop or Adjustable Setpoint were reached at Pmin or Pmax. 

This trapped the gas between the wellhead and the control valve stopping the normal convection flows of warmer gas between the caverns. 

If the ambient temperature was below zero this static gas would cool to 0 degrees and activate the low temperature wellhead trip which is only intended to prevent low gas temperatures in the cavern and production tubing caused by a large, prolonged withdrawal.

To remedy this problem the trip was made ‘smart’ and was only activated if the flow control valve was open and it was deactivated when the valve was closed and no withdrawal could be occurring but this required a closed limit indication adding to the actuators. (see attached)

Since then 8 replacement actuator controllers were ordered that don’t come with the limits as standard and they have been in the stores for some time until one was fitted on H403 and were identified that the limits (there may have been an open limit fitted too) were missing.

The absence of the closed limit switch would not create a hazard and it would just generate the potential for an unnecessary trip.

This has been recorded as it is a case of a like for like replacement that isn’t.
TITLE: Like for like actuator issue

CASE_DESCRIPTION:
An initial problem was detected with the GRUs where they were quickly dumping >6m3 hour of cold teg into the regen units on start up, which if wet could lead to a pressure trip. A modification was prepared for tuning out some poor control on the flow limiter on the stripping column.  However, it was not implemented because on closer inspection, the Rich TEG buffer vessel level Operator-adjustable set point was sitting at a low level.  Increasing the set point from 380 mm to 500 mm smoothed the start up process and prevented the pressure trips.

After a period of time, Operators detected that during the shut down of the GRUs, the TEG HP pumps were repeatedly turning on and off.  Investigation identified that this was because the auto-changeover setpoint of 1m3/hr was now being matched by the flow of Rich TEG from the buffer tank due to the changed setpoint (as described above).

There was no safety consequence to the pumps repeatedly changing over.  However, there was a potential plant damage risk.  Hence, this observation has been raised to determine any additional learning relating to the sites control of modification set points, including operator adjustable set points.
TITLE: Unanticipated effect from altered Operator set point

CASE_DESCRIPTION:
There have been multiple cases of low level hydrogen leaks detected on both SC10 and SC20 synchronous condensers during offline periods.

July 7th 2022

The synchronous condenser was shutdown due to the need for a Mod 2 400KV grid isolation for maintenance activities.

Whilst the SC20 Generator was at standstill a hydrogen leak alarm was received on the gas detector panel CYE01 in the Killingholme control room. Investigations at that time could not detect a genuine leak although the reading appeared to last for approximately 30 seconds and peaked at 20% LEL. This alarm was detected at both ends of the Generator on both HD005 and HD006. 

Later as the Hydrogen Purity Concentration procedure was being carried out these alarms were received again. This time a noticeable leak could be heard within the turbine hall also. These readings peaked at 40% LEL and the detection lasted for several minutes. 

To clarify the first alarm was received with the shaft at standstill and no work being carried out and the second alarm was received when the shaft was still at standstill but hydrogen filling was taking place.

A further leak alarm was detected when  SC20 was put on barring up to 200RPM using the oil system

Aug 21st 2022

Again a 400KV outage was required for maintenance activities on MOD1.

Again, Killingholme OPS took the opportunity to attempt to sweeten the generator hydrogen purity. There were similar leaks of hydrogen detected as there was on SC20 above but in slightly different.

* Whilst at standstill during the H2 sweetening process

* Whilst at standstill following completion of the sweetening process.

* Whilst on barring on the return to operation

19/12/2022

Leak alarms were once again raised when SC20 was stopped to carry out repairs on GT21 GCB.  Leaks stopped once the unit was put back on barring.
TITLE: SC10/20 Generator Hydrogen Leak alarms.

CASE_DESCRIPTION:
Recently at Ratcliffe we've taken delivery of 600 new HID access control cards.  As of last month our previously issued E.On access control cards ran out and we started issuing from the new batch.

After a few days a couple of users informed us that when setting up SecurePrint on their new cards, when scanning in on the printers instead of taking them through the registration process it logged them in as another user.

We believe that this is due to the stored numbers on the two active people's different cards being the same, and/or SecurePrint not using the site code portion of the access control cards.

This is a data protection risk as there is a chance that these users with duplicate card numbers could print sensitieve personal data off the SecurePrint queue from that account that they are incorrectly logged into.

I've attached a flow diagram to explain the problem.

Fundamentally we believe that the fragmented way that Access Control cards are issued across the company and having a company wide access control card swipe system for the printers is why the risk of duplicate numbers on Access control cards is a data protection risk.

There is also a potential that these duplicate cards could allow someone access to another site that they are not authorised, but we don't believe this risk is high as the access control systems should use the site codes as well, but this will need investigating.
TITLE: Potential for Duplicate Swipe Card Numbers to be allocated with different Access Control Cards

CASE_DESCRIPTION:
During a run up to FSNL. _x000D_
21:22 Bearing 2 vib > max 1 alarm. DCS showed 20mm/s but this is the max of its range. GE suggested the GT should have tripped automatically but it didn't. _x000D_
21:23 GT reached FSNL and vibration has dropped_x000D_
_x000D_
The reason for the GT not tripping on high vibration was investigated. The Bentley Nevada set points were checked and the trip levels are set at 14.7 when the GT trip matrix says they should be 11.8. With the 1.5x mulitplier on start up the 14.7 became 22.05 which was above the range of the instrument (20mm/s) so the GT did not trip. Once at FSNL the multipliers are not in effect so the trip limit was back to 14.7. _x000D_
_x000D_
Further investigation required.
TITLE: GT vibration trip setting

As part of the preparation (09/02), the operative laid out the cable to check its identification. Due to the location of the gland plate and the termination point, approximately 4m of cable was laid out. The operative laid the cable out, on the floor to the wall end of the PCC and was returning to the works location, when he heard an arcing sound. The operative turned around to see the cable sparking between the switchroom wall and a cabinet.
The operative called to his work partner (located on a different part of the PCC) and both operatives moved away and called for assistance.

No injuries sustained.
TITLE: SC20 PCC Low Voltage Switchroom Incident

CASE_DESCRIPTION:
The safety isolation key for the Upsurge Control Valve No.515 Control Air valve was released from the T3B cascade key safe following the return of the T3B PFW.  The release of this key (safety key No 9727) allowed us to prepare for the PFW ROMP (Permit For Work with Restoration Of Motive Power), for the re-connection of the valve 515 and setting of the valve limits.   Following release of the key on the morning of the 13/07, the Outage Commissioning operative was asked to attach a ROMP notice to the valve in preparation for the issue of the safety document.  On getting to the valve location it was noted that there was no isolation lock on the valve as expected.  The chain that was used to isolate the valve was still attached to the valve body / pipework but there was no sign of the isolation lock.
The control valve and actuator had both been removed & replaced during the Outage period.  The air pipework and the valve spindle had both been disconnected to allow the removal / replacement of the valve / actuator.  The air isolation valve was not directly local to the valve, it was the master isolator approx 6ft away on the adjacent wall.
The Authorised Persons Isolation sheet was checked, and the isolation point had been double checked and double signed for at the start of the Outage period when the T3B cascade box was established; on release of the safety key from the key safe the signatures were crossed off of the AP sheet.  The immediate area was searched for any sign of a broken / damaged lock, but nothing could be found.
TITLE: U4 Upsurge Control Valve No515 Control Air Valve missing isolation lock

CASE_DESCRIPTION:
A PFW safety document for U4 ‘Y’ 3.3KV SW/BRD maintenance was issued on Monday 16th May (AM) to one of the electrical CP’s.

The CP (Competent Person) proceeded to work on the 3.3KV ‘Y’ board during the coarse of the day, carrying out VCB maintenance, CCT spout maintenance and function checks as per his maintenance orders and maintenance procedures and PFW.  At the end of the working day the CP surrendered the PFW and explained to the duty SAP (Senior Authorised Person) the state of the works and progress made.  During the discussion the CP stated that the VCB’s had been returned to the Earth position.  
To allow the VCB’s to return to the CCT earth position, requires the 110v solenoid fuses to be available; but the duty SAP noted the fuses were quoted as a POI on the safety document.

In discussion with the SAP who prepared the safety document - During the preparation stage, he had read & understood that the electrical method, stated 110v supplies were needed to function check the VCB closing springs, & that the VCB’s should be returned to the as found position following cct spout maintenance.  

Because of this, the preparing SAP had made supplies available to the 110V solenoids for function checking, and to allow the VCB’s to be put back to the CCT earth position.  The Safety document was already pre-prepared on Nisoft quoting the Solenoid fuses as POI’s, and the Preparing SAP omitted to remove the isolation point from the POI’s list in Nisoft prior to printing.  

The safety document was cancelled and the POI on Nisoft quoting the Solenoid 110v fuses was removed.   The new Safety document was re-issued on the 17th May to continue the work.

The isolation point originally quoted – 
•	‘Y’ Unit SW/BRD 110v CONTROL FUSES & SOLENOID FUSES             WITHDRAWN & CAUTIONED

The isolation point was changed to  
•	‘Y’ Unit SW/BRD 110v CONTROL FUSES                                              
WITHDRAWN & CAUTIONED

The safety document had been pre-prepared so that an isolation list could be produced for the isolating AP.  This was a couple of weeks prior to the document being printed as the contractors were delayed in attending site.

The Solenoid isolation had been removed from the key safe, made available & crossed off of the AP sheet by the preparing SAP, but not removed from the PFW.

Please note that this Observation Synergy is being raised as a prompt to have a discussion regarding the importance of SAP's to ensure the  administrative preparation of the safety documents is given the SAP's full attention, and is prioritised, to ensure the SAP isn't distracted by non SFS procedures.
TITLE: U4 'Y' 3.3KV Switchboard

QEB10AA153 Short Description: U4 A AFCU STRM 2 SHUTOFF ISOL VLV
QEB10AA153 Long Description: U4 A SIDE SCR AMMONIA FLOW CONTROL UNIT STREAM 2 SHUTOFF VALVE INSTRUMENT AIR SUPPLY ISOLATION VALVE

HSJ10AA010 Short Description: U4 A AFCU STRM 2 PNEU SOV 
HSJ10AA010 Long Description: A SIDE SCR AMMONIA FLOW CONTROL UNIT STREAM 2 PNEUMATIC SHUTOFF VALVE

The associated permit (already cancelled) 2022/2309/SP used a correct functional location description for the work intended although did not reference KKS HSJ10AA010 :

TITLE: SSOW - U4 AFCU Steam 2 Shut Off Valve - Notification & WOC with incorrect SAP FL

Followed the leak to Turbine floor: Oil was found to be spraying from test pressure gauge on ST IP Stop Valve North Side.

Leak from hot surfaces and surrounding areas then cleaned, pipes lagging inspected and claddings cleaned from leaked & accumulated oil in lagging insulation,  

Gas turbine was kept ON during this time on bypass mode. Once the oil leak was rectified, REMIT declared and unit was brought back to base load.

CASE_DESCRIPTION: A leak occurred on HRSG transmitter 01FSR54CFT, To identify leak it was required to shut away isolation valves as unable to get close to steam leak to identify. Isolation valves were identified on PID as 01FSRHV926 & HV927. Valve locations identified on plant and valves with these labels were closed. on closing 01FSRHV927 it was observed that 'A' transmitter was lost on DCS and leak did not stop. This valve was reopened and reading returned to normal on 'A' transmitter. In the area are all isolation valves for 'A' , 'B' and 'C' transmitter, some valves had no labels and by visually inspecting it was not clear which valves were pairs. It was possible to identify which valve was HV927 through process of elimination until leak stopped at flow transmitter 'C', valve label FSRHV927 removed from wrong valve (Label was actually around cladding adjacent to valve). It is unclear if all other valves are correct and will require further testing to ensure all labels are correct on all units (Valve locations slightly different on other units)
TITLE: Valve incorrectly labelled

CASE_DESCRIPTION:
On Monday 27th September at approx 0830, a Permit For Work ROMP ( Restoration of Motive Power) was issued from the Outage permit for work office to allow the set-up of limits and stroking of pneumatic valve 255 following outage works.  At the time of issue the boiler was being set up for a Hydraulic test.  As per normal procedure and prior to the hydraulic, all issued docs were checked and any relevant safety documents that could affect the hydraulic were suspended.  Between the times of the check of the issued documents and start of the boiler hydraulic, the ROMP for valve 255 was issued without the issuing SAP making the connection to it being affected by the boiler hydraulic.  The CP who collected the Romp proceeded to his point of work, made the air supply available and started to stroke the valve from the local junction box.  As the valve opened there was a release of pressure within the process pipework, which was 'quite loud' and caused vibration within the pipework.  This startled the CP and he proceeded to shut the control air valve immediately.   The CP reported straight to the Outage duty SAP who attended the point of work and realised the ROMP should not have been in force during the boiler hydraulic test.  The ROMP was suspended and working party withdrawn.   

The PFW ROMP specifically stated no access to the process side of the control valve / system, so the CP and working party were not at risk from the process medium.
TITLE: U1 Boiler HP Sootblower Control Valve 255.

CASE_DESCRIPTION:
ST Clutch Lube Oil supply pipe weld was commenced on Sunday morning 30th august 2020. _x000D_
On cutting the existing pipe the Doosan Tech saw more oil than he was expecting draining under head from the stub pipe he had cut, not under pressure just weiring over. _x000D_
He stopped work ,informed us and we went to investigate. _x000D_
There was quite a bit of oil in the gallery under the grating. We applied a spill kit and requested Wayne Chandler to assist cleaning it up with spill pads. _x000D_
There was about 10 litres of oil possibly that we mopped up and it stopped flowing from the stub._x000D_
We conducted a job stop and meeting with GE supervisor. jacking oil work was suspended while we established a cause._x000D_
_x000D_
 The reason for the oil draining from the pipework was the fact that the bearing pedestals had filled with oil because of the jacking oil being put into service constantly. The level would reach the supply pipework internally to the pedestal._x000D_
This then ran down the SUPPLY pipework, filling the blanked and previously drained line back to the tank.. _x000D_
It was drain under head only and a gentle weiring from the stub. It would drain and stop . when jacking oil back in service a little bit more would drain._x000D_
_x000D_
We fitted a drain hose to the cut stub pipe and this was placed into an IBC to collect any oil. Permit for Clutch supply pipe weld cancelled._x000D_
 Monday 31st August the line was drained at the supply blank and the blank removed . Lube oil pumps isolated and PFW issued to weld flange onto stub after line proved drained again.._x000D_
 _x000D_
 History;_x000D_
Supply pipework drained and Lube oil blank fitted under PFW 2020/00819 on 01/08/2020 and entered into blanks register._x000D_
Drain /return lines back to tank remained available throughout._x000D_
This was the basis for our Clutch weld job._x000D_
Clutch weld job PFW2020/ 00945 issued 15/08/2020(proved drained) work allowed to commence 30/08/2020 (drained line now contained oil).
TITLE: Excessive oil from drained pipework

CASE_DESCRIPTION: During the morning commute to work I observed a Grey Audi A3, registration YM19 WNU driving very dangerously. Whilst exiting the M1 northbound at junction 24 the Audi driver decided not to join the slip road in advance and instead continued travelling in the bottom lane of the M1 making no indication that he would be exiting at the junction. He then decided that he needed to leave the M1 at J24 and dangerously came to a stop in the bottom lane of the M1 which made other drivers travelling at speed of up to 70mph take evasive action to avoid a serious collision. The driver then proceeded to make his way around the J24 roundabout towards the A453. At the traffic lights leading to the A453 (remembrance way) the driver decided to cut in front of me where there was clearly insufficient space causing me to take emergency action. The driver clearly believed that his actions were justified as when I sounded my horn he replied with a 'gesture'. I overtook the driver on the A453 and continued into the UTG carpark. I realised that the Audi driver was also travelling to site and as I parked up I saw him drive at excessive speeds between the gatehouse and the Engineering Academy which was his end destination. Within 5 minutes this driver caused 3 separate incidents on the road, all of which had the potential to be fatal.
TITLE: Dangerous Driving

CASE_DESCRIPTION: A Trainer was attending a customer site to complete apprentice observations. He arrived at site on 22nd September and completed a successful transfer to and from the wind turbine. The following day the waves were high and RWE were in a position where they were deciding whether or not to go off shore. A decision was made to go ahead. Later in the day the team at RWE were told they had to leave the turbine within an hour and a half because the waves were getting high. The team transferred and all made it back to site safely however, Jonathan has described it as a frightening experience. RWE state safe wave height should be 2.8m but the waves on this day were over 3m. When they returned to site all RWE staff were asked to complete near hits so that they could investigate the reasons someone had authorised transfer to the wind turbine that day. As the Trainer was part of the group on site and for his own safety we wanted to raise this as a near hit within Uniper too.
TITLE: Transferring - Offshore wind turbine

• HE Project Team engaged IT last year on the scope and delivery requirements._x000D_
• The original agreed completion date for all IT works was w/c 23 March._x000D_
• The project team were informed on the day the IT project should have been delivered that it is now 2 months late (potentially 3 to full completion)_x000D_
•  An order for a dedicated 100mb BT broadband line with a 60d ay lead time had not been processed._x000D_
•  IT were engaging a 3 person family contract business_x000D_
• The late delivery leaves operations with a contract claims risk. _x000D_
• The operations team is now having to organise elements on the installation to get things moving.
TITLE: Lack of progress with IT connections that has now created a significant operational risk associated with the HE project at Enfield

CASE_DESCRIPTION:
A HGSL Operator is developing a simulator of the control system.  This work requires systematic review of the alarm arrangements across the installation.  When reviewing smoke and gas detection within the compressor enclosures, the Operator noticed that the code for the compressor to "fail safe" in the event of detector power-loss did not reflect the arrangement elsewhere on the site.  Hence, based on the operators concern that the detectors were not "fail safe", testing was undertaken on the same day to isolate the power and review the function of the code.  The test identified that the detectors were fail safe, but used a slightly different code - most likely due to the automatic EDP function found on the compressors but not elsewhere on the plant._x000D_
_x000D_
This report has been raised to document both the findings of the test and to note the potential benefit in such proactive alarm reviews.

CASE_DESCRIPTION:
NDT/Radiography has been completed on a number of shifts – the process involves completing the Appendix A documentation which details important information – one being the source type and size – the source decay certificate also states type and current size – the Appendix A is prepared by the FieldCore Mechanical contractor along with the decay certificate – this is checked/signed by the Uniper Engineer and distributed to relevant parties nominated on the Appendix A – the source nominated was Iridium - Ir192 23.7._x000D_
Iris the NDT company arrived at Enfield Power station at approx. 02:00 – after a review the Shift team leader found the source was a Selenium 75 Source with a strength of 32.8 Curies. (>20Curies) – The shift team leader has been on Nights since Wednesday, I was confident in the competence of the IRIS Engineers and decided this was admin error and not that IRIS had bought the wrong Source._x000D_
Once IRIS showed the shift team leader all the necessary paperwork for the Source, he allowed the Radiography to continue._x000D_
The fact that IRIS told him during the Saturday morning testing, that they were bringing a stronger Selenium Source for Sunday’s testing, was also taken in to account.
TITLE: Incorrect paper work detailing type of radioactive NDT source planned to be used on weld testing

CASE_DESCRIPTION:
I went to Ratcliffe Power Station to carry out internal visual inspection of the U3 main steam drum (part of the 2020 Statutory outage works).  This pressure vessel is classed as a “confined space”._x000D_
_x000D_
Prior to entry, we were informed by staff from the mechanical contractor that there was no requirement to wear any gas monitoring / detection equipment.  The mechanical contracting staff were working in the vessel when we arrived, however they exited the vessel to enable us to carry out our inspection work._x000D_
_x000D_
Before commencing work, we confirmed the lack of gas monitor requirement with a visit to the permit office / control room._x000D_
_x000D_
However, because a gas monitor is specified in our RAMS, we sourced a gas monitor from the Station Chemist and conducted our work as usual with a gas monitor attached._x000D_
_x000D_
This appeared to be an apparent change to the sites procedures.  Personal gas monitoring / detection equipment has been considered mandatory in confined spaces of this nature in previous years and at every other site UTG work on.   _x000D_
_x000D_
We believe the Station has conducted a full investigation, therefore this is more for UTG learning.
TITLE: Ratcliffe Confined Space Procedures

CASE_DESCRIPTION:
On Friday 17th September it was reported that a GE/Fieldcore operative could not smell the wd40 he was using, as a precaution he took a LFT which proved positive, he left site in a controlled manner and the area sanitised, a close contact assessment completed. (He was a few days later confirmed positive by the official PCR).
3 operatives where identified and each had a LFT which all proved negative, they all had been double jabbed and were assessed able to carry on working as per Government advice.
However this against EGTL site procedure and against the instruction of the Grain Safety Team Leader who was contacted on A/L. The EGTL procedure insists that all Close Contacts should have been isolated until such time that the EGTL Appendix 9 RTW for Close Contacts had been completed. 
The Safety Team Leader did not find out until Tuesday 21st that the Close Contacts had been allowed to stay at work.
LFT have been conducted daily on the Close Contacts and surveillance and controls in place and negative results recorded.
TITLE: Coronavirus Close Contact Assessment breach of EGTL COVID-19 Procedure.

CASE_DESCRIPTION:
A crane lift, of  sheeting panels onto U42 were witnessed without a tag line fitted. This caused the panels on both occasions to spin and bump into the side of the access platform and structure. No injury or damaged sustained.
Several staff members witnessed the incident and intervened.
The panel was blowing about and started to spin. The driver in the cherry picker moved his basket in to the panel to stop it spinning around so he could control it and place the panel where it needed to go. Whilst several of the witnesses set off  to speak to the working party, they started lifting another panel so they decided to let them finish. As the panel was being lifted they noticed that there wasn’t a tagline attached. Again, the panel started blowing about and was slammed in to the steel work of the enclosure, the panel struck the steel work another 2 times before the driver in the cherry picker could control it. Two of witnesses went and spoke to the rigging crew and supervisor on the ground who were stood watching the lift, they were asked to use a tag line, which was about 2m away. The lifting party were reminded that if it’s too windy, don’t carry out the lift.
TITLE: Lifting of a load without a tag line fitted.

CASE_DESCRIPTION:
On Sunday 23rd May 2021, a Competent person (CP) collected a safety document PFW ROMP (Restoration Of Motive Power) to work on bled steam to de-aerator valve 4002.   Following collection of the safety document, the CP proceeded to the point of work he knew as 4002 valve, but found that the safety key issued with the PFW ROMP did not match the isolation lock on the valve, and there wasn't a ROMP notice present.  
The CP contacted the duty Senior Authorised Person (SAP) immediately to report his findings.  The SAP attended the point of work and found the CP on what he believed to be the wrong valve.  The CP confirmed through his experience and knowledge that he believed he was on 4002 valve, and showed the SAP a handwritten sign on the pneumatic valve control box (approximately 12ft away from the valve it's self) stating it was valve 4002.  The duty SAP took the CP to the valve that was isolated for the ROMP, and showed him the local permanent plant ID label attached to the valve stating valve 4002.  After some discussion and consulting drawings, it was still not 100% clear which valve was 4002.  The Duty SAP cancelled the PFW ROMP and de-isolated both 4001 & 4002 valves, and asked a Unit Operator to operate the valves remotely from the ovation soft desk in the main control room.  On operation of the valves it was confirmed that the permanent plant ID label attached to U4 4002 valve was incorrect, and that the valve was actually 4001.  

After confirming that the identification on valve 4001 (stating 4002) was wrong, 4002 valve was inspected and there was no plant label attached to 4002 valve, apart from the hand written sign on the pneumatic control box which is not local to the valve. 

U4 is currently on an Interim outage, and the air supply valves for both 4001 and 4002 were isolated at the start of the outage period (approx. 2 weeks earlier).  Both valves have been worked on through the outage with 4002 requiring setting up under a PFW ROMP before being returned to service.

Information

Both 4001 and 4002 pneumatic bled steam valves are located on U4 De-aerator.  On Unit 4, 4001 valve is located on the 'B' side of the De-aerator, 4002 is located on the 'A' side.  The valves are approximately 10 meters apart, each on it's own platform.  The valves are the opposite way round on U1 & U2 compared to U3 & U4.
TITLE: SSoW - U4 pneumatic bled steam to DA valve 4002 permit for work ROMP

CASE_DESCRIPTION:
Whilst withdrawing gas from the caverns and changing load from 700,000Sm3/hr to 900,000Sm3/hr by the pressure reduction valves (PRV’s) the plant suffered an unexpected Safety Instrumented System (SIS) trip on rate of change (falling <1bar/min) on the pipeline to the National transmission system (NTS)._x000D_
_x000D_
In 2011 similar issues were experienced when certain plant conditions were met (approx. 8 bar dp between caverns and the National Transmission System [NTS] system). To prevent this from occurring a Management of Change (MoC) was implemented that allowed the shift operator control of the plant 'global gain'. This global gain effectively slows the plant control system down to prevent these large flow variances happening quickly and thus preventing demands on the SIS system. There is a standing operational instruction for the shift operator to manually change the global gain from 1 to 0.7 when in these pressure ranges._x000D_
_x000D_
On this occasion the operator had not reduced the global gain as when the withdrawal nomination commenced the conditions for the global gain to be reduced were not met, however, as these conditions are dynamic as the withdrawal nomination continued the conditions were met but the global gain was not adjusted._x000D_
_x000D_
Upon investigation of the DCS trend it appears this has been happening (to a lesser extent) for the past 16 months. This ties in with a rolling programme of overhauling each PRV, of which we have 3 off. It is thought that splitting the flow across two valves instead of three may have contributed to the issues described.
TITLE: Loss of process control resulting in plant trip

CASE_DESCRIPTION:
It appears that U6 Sequencers (HRSG/WSC and ST) stopped running(Disabled themselves) when restarting the unit from an SSD trip during unit start-up. _x000D_
It was not noticed that the sequencers were not running initially (no alarms) until the operator realised that the HP bypass had failed to open. Immediately the HP by-pass was manually switched on which resulted in the HP-pass opening to pressurise the cold re-heat line as designed. This had the result of pressurising the CRH line due to high pressure already in the HP steam line. this consequently led to the CRH safety valves lifting at their designed lift pressures. _x000D_
Just after the HP-bypass had been switched on it was then noticed that the HRSG/WSC and ST sequencers were not running, these were immediately re-started. Once the condenser vacuum had reached 300mbar, the CRH pressure was able to relieve to the condenser via the IP by-pass valve. The unit the ran up as designed.
TITLE: Uncontrolled Release of steam via safety valve.

CASE_DESCRIPTION:

The operatives were scaffolding around the drive end of U1 61, so were in close proximity to U2 No62.  This particular style of Sootblower (of which there are at least 8 on section 2 per unit) have a section of unguarded shaft on the side of the drive end.  The Operatives were in close proximity to the unguarded rotating shaft and were installing supports directly below it.  The operative immediately reported this to their supervisor and the working party withdrew from the area.
There has been an assessment of the same design of Sootblower across unit 1 & 2 and all Sootblowers of this type have an approx 30" section of exposed shaft, of which at least 4 are at an accessible height on a walkway adjacent to a main stairwell.
The shafts do spin relatively slowly
Please note these are original design Sootblowers that have been installed and used for the station life, and I understand they have never been guarded.
TITLE: U1 61 Sootblower.

CASE_DESCRIPTION:
DMW Analyst was carrying out the routine personal dust monitoring on the Altrad stripping team when they noticed an amount of dust in the atmosphere inside the asbestos tent._x000D_
The pump was worn for a duration of 40 minutes at 2 litres per min. The limit of detection for this personal was 0.06 fibres per ml, the calculated result was 0.31 fibres per ml after a reading of 100.5 fibres on the slide in 33 fields. This is a fail by a large margin._x000D_
After speaking to the ALTRAD supervisors, they have informed me their limit of detection is 0.50 fibres per ml, so the result for them is not a fail, but they have acknowledged the reading is unsatisfactory, so a tool box talk will be conducted with Altrad staff._x000D_
